articles.title: ‘We are asking for equal opportunity’: Para cyclists  protest over Asian Para Games selection
articles.summary: New Delhi: A selection row has erupted in Indian para cycling with athletes planning a protest at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium on Thursday after only a
articles.body: New Delhi: A selection row has erupted in Indian para cycling with athletes planning a protest at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium on Thursday after only a single individual — Arshad Shaikh — was included in the final contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.The development comes after six para cyclists had earlier been unanimously recommended for the event by the Cycling Federation of India (CFI) and Paralympic Committee of India’s (PCI) joint selection committee in its Aug 28 meeting.Shaikh (MC2 sports category), Pavan Kumar Kommoji (MC3), Sameer (MC4), Prashant Arkal (MH4), Vishva Vasani (WC3) and Lisha Das (WC4) were the names originally shortlisted. Their selection was based on performance, minimum qualifying standards (MQS), Asian/Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) rankings and international qualification.The athletes say the process reducing six recommended cyclists to one has not been explained. “We are asking for equal opportunity based on performance, qualification and merit,” they said in a joint mail to authorities, seeking athlete-wise reasons and criteria.They say they bore international expenses, equipment and prosthetic costs themselves. A total of 14 able-bodied cyclists were selected for the just-concluded able-bodied Asian Games. The para cycling team is due to leave for Japan on Oct 13, with their classification begins Oct 14 and events run from Oct 19-22.The 2025 Asian rankings showed Shaikh first/6th in road/track events, Kommoji 3rd/3rd in road/track, Sameer 3rd/5th in road/track, Arkal 2nd in road; Vasani 2nd/3rd in road/track and Das 3rd/2nd in road/track.In 2026, the positions were Shaikh 2nd/3rd in road/track, Kommoji 2nd/3rd, Sameer 8th/5th, Arkal 2nd, Vasani 3rd/2nd and Das 6th/2nd. Track rankings do not apply to MH4 category.India was sixth in men’s and fourth in women’s Asian UCI Nations Rankings on Feb 2, 2026. articles.title: Asian Para Games send-off marred by protests over selection process
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games send-off ceremony was overshadowed by protests by para-shooters and para-cyclists here on Thursday, with
articles.body: New Delhi: The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games send-off ceremony was overshadowed by protests by para-shooters and para-cyclists here on Thursday, with athletes demanding fairness in selection for the multisport event, scheduled from Oct 18-24.As the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) held the ceremony at a city hotel in the presence of sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya, para shooters gathered outside the hotel lobby with placards and banners. Some protesters, including shooters Sandeep Kumar and Akash, had demonstrated at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium on Wednesday.The protesters were initially dispersed by hotel security and later requested by Delhi Police personnel to leave as demonstrations were not permitted inside the premises. It is learnt that the minister wanted to meet them and discuss their concerns. He asked officials to check whether they were still around and waited in the lobby, but was informed that they had left.The minister then held discussions with ministry and Sports Authority of India (SAI) officials, with sources saying he stressed that the selection process should be fair and transparent.PCI president Devendra Jhajharia later defended the selections, saying PCI, ministry and SAI guidelines had been followed. He said athletes’ concerns had been heard and would be discussed with the ministry and PCI board, while leaving open the possibility of a review.Meanwhile, aggrieved para cyclists staged a protest outside Gate No. 1 of JLN stadium, demanding a fair selection. Arshad Shaikh, the lone cyclist selected for the contingent, joined his unselected teammates at the protest. A cyclists’ representative later met SAI officials at its headquarters in the evening and raised concerns over the exclusion of other recommended cyclists and its impact on India’s medal and Paralympic qualification prospects.The selection committee had recommended six cyclists, but only Shaikh made the contingent, prompting questions over the criteria used to reduce the list.Payal’s coach omission adds another concernLeading para archer Payal Nag’s coach Abhilasha Vedwan has been left out of the contingent, it’s been learnt. Payal has urged PCI to allow Abhilasha to travel, saying her medal prospects could suffer without her coach. Only Pankaj Singh and Gaurav Sharma have been approved as para archery coaches. Para badminton coach Gaurav Khanna has also been left out.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Para cyclists’ protest enters Day 2, even sole Asian Para Games pick joins stir
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Para Games fast approaching, India’s para cyclists are spending their days demanding answers instead of focusing on their
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Para Games fast approaching, India’s para cyclists are spending their days demanding answers instead of focusing on their preparations, as their protest against the team selection entered its second consecutive day on Friday.The cyclists continued their sit-in outside Gate No. 1 of Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium, braving the harsh sun and sitting on the pavement to demand justice and the inclusion of the athletes they say were overlooked despite meeting the selection criteria. Their grievance remains unchanged: six cyclists were recommended by the joint selection committee of the Cycling Federation of India (CFI) and Paralympic Committee of India (PCI), but only one — Arshad Shaikh — made the final contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.Even Shaikh, the lone cyclist selected, has joined the protest in solidarity with his fellow athletes. Instead of concentrating solely on his training and preparations for the continental event, he is standing alongside those questioning why they were left out.The athletes allege that their repeated appeals have failed to elicit a satisfactory response from the authorities. They want the selection decision reconsidered and a clear explanation of why the other recommended cyclists were excluded. The protesters say they will continue their agitation until their demands are met and the sidelined athletes are considered for selection.The dispute stems from the joint selection committee’s August 28 meeting, at which six cyclists were unanimously recommended for the Games. The list comprised Shaikh (MC2), Pavan Kumar Kommoji (MC3), Sameer (MC4), Prashant Arkal (MH4), Vishva Vasani (WC3) and Lisha Das (WC4).According to the athletes, their recommendations were based on performances, minimum qualifying standards, Asian and Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) rankings, and international qualification criteria. They have sought athlete-wise explanations and clarity on the basis on which the final list was reduced from six names to one.The cyclists have also pointed to the financial burden they have borne, claiming to have met expenses related to international participation, equipment and prosthetics themselves. With the Games looming, they argue that the uncertainty over their selection has added to the strain on athletes who should be preparing to represent the country.The Asian rankings cited by the athletes show that several of the excluded cyclists had competitive positions in their respective categories. In 2026, Shaikh was ranked second in road and third in track, while Kommoji was second and third, respectively. Sameer was eighth in road and fifth in track; Arkal was second in road; Vasani was third in road and second in track; and Das was sixth in road and second in track. Track rankings do not apply to the MH4 category.The athletes have also cited India’s position in the Asian UCI Nations Rankings as part of their argument over qualification slots, seeking transparency on how the available places were allocated.The cyclists’ protest comes amid wider discontent over selections for the Asian Para Games. Para-shooters have also continued to raise objections over the selection process. On Thursday, their protest at the Indian contingent’s send-off ceremony brought allegations of irregularities and favouritism into focus, with athletes questioning their exclusion from the squad. The allegations have been contested by officials, who have maintained that selection was based on the prescribed criteria.With both groups raising concerns over selection transparency, the protests have cast a shadow over India’s preparations for the Games. For the cyclists outside JLN stadium, however, the immediate demand remains simple: an explanation for the decision, a fair hearing and a resolution before the team departs for Japan.“We will continue our protest until our demands are met,” the cyclists have maintained.For athletes who should be sharpening their competitive edge ahead of a major international event, the question now is how long they will have to remain on the pavement before their pleas are heard.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Carrying the tricolour is a different feeling’: Pramod Bhagat eyes gold at Para Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For a champion who has conquered the biggest stages in para badminton, the prospect of carrying the Indian flag as the flagbearer at the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For a champion who has conquered the biggest stages in para badminton, the prospect of carrying the Indian flag as the flagbearer at the upcoming Para Asian Games for Pramod Bhagat is still an experience that stands apart from every medal and accolade.A gold medallist at the Tokyo Paralympics, Bhagat is preparing for his fifth Asian Para Games, carrying with him the experience of six medals, including two golds and four bronze. Yet, despite years of competing at the highest level, the responsibility of carrying the tricolour has brought a fresh sense of excitement.Bhagat recalled watching flag bearers lead the Indian contingent during his earlier appearances at the continental showpiece. The sight left a lasting impression on him, and now, as he prepares to take on that role himself, the feeling has become all the more meaningful.Having already won Paralympic gold, two Asian Games gold medals and the Padma Shri, Bhagat has experienced several defining moments in his sporting journey. However, he believes that the honour of being flag bearer cannot be compared with any of those achievements.“My expectation is gold, but it won't be easy,” he said, underlining the ambition that continues to drive him despite an already impressive medal collection.For Bhagat, longevity at the highest level has been built on the ability to adapt. Every edition of the Asian Para Games brings a different set of challenges, with opponents improving, preparations changing and the demands of the sport becoming more intense.“When you go to the second or third Asian Para Games, there is a difference of four years. A lot changes in four years. I try to learn from the past and move forward. I try to do my best, and I want to be successful,” he said.That approach has helped Bhagat remain a key figure in India's para badminton movement. His focus is not simply on defending his reputation but on finding ways to improve with every campaign. The target remains gold, but the process involves learning from previous performances, understanding the competition and making the most of his preparation.Beyond his personal ambitions, Bhagat is equally encouraged by the growing strength of Indian para badminton. With the sport attracting greater attention and Indian athletes making their presence felt internationally, expectations have risen.The goal, he said, is to push the country's medal count even higher.“We want to win more than 10 medals in the Para Asian Games,” Bhagat said, reflecting the confidence within the Indian contingent.The optimism is backed by a broader upward trend in India's para-sports performance. Bhagat pointed to the country's growing medal tally, noting that India had crossed the 100-medal mark at the previous Asian Para Games. For him, the progress is evidence of how sustained support, improved facilities and greater visibility can translate into results on the field.He believes the transformation has been particularly noticeable compared with the early days of his career, when govt assistance and public recognition for para badminton were more limited.Bhagat credited the government's growing involvement and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for taking a personal interest in para badminton, which he said had helped bring the sport greater recognition and publicity. That visibility, in turn, encouraged private organisations to come forward and support athletes.“When you get good support, and your equipment and training facilities improve, you perform well,” he said.The backing from both the government and the private sector, Bhagat believes, has helped create a stronger ecosystem for para athletes. Better equipment, improved training infrastructure and greater exposure have given players more opportunities to prepare and compete at the highest level. The rising medal count, he said, reflects the difference that such support can make.As India looks to build on its achievements at the continental level, Bhagat's campaign carries significance beyond the medals he hopes to win. He represents a generation of athletes who have benefited from a changing sporting environment while helping raise the profile of para badminton through their performances.For the veteran shuttler, though, the immediate task remains clear: prepare well, learn from experience and pursue gold. The flag-bearing honour has added another dimension to his campaign, giving him a responsibility that goes beyond his individual events.Bhagat knows that success will not come easily, but he is ready to embrace the challenge. And when he leads the Indian contingent with the tricolour in his hands, the moment will represent more than the achievements of a champion. It will reflect the journey of Indian para badminton, the progress of its athletes and the pride of representing the country.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ban threat on para shooters for challenging PCI in court
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With India’s Asian Para Games preparations already marred by selection disputes and court battles, the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) has
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With India’s Asian Para Games preparations already marred by selection disputes and court battles, the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) has landed in another controversy over a para shooting policy that threatens athletes with lengthy bans for challenging its decisions in court.A clause in the PCI governing body-approved 2026-27 national selection policy for para shooting prescribes a three-year ban if a shooter or their parents initiate legal action against the association and the case is dismissed. A repeat offence could invite a lifetime ban, according to the 16-page policy, a copy of which is with TOI.“Any para shooters/coaches/parents going to the courts or taking any legal action against the association and further if the case is dismissed by the court, the para shooter would be banned for at least three years and in case of repeated offence, ban could go for lifetime as well,” the clause states.The provision raises questions about athletes’ right to seek judicial redress in selection disputes, potentially exposing para shooters to severe sporting sanctions for challenging the PCI’s decisions.A senior PCI official told TOI that the clause was damaging and should never have been included. The official said directions had been issued to amend the policy and that a corrigendum would be uploaded. However, since the policy was approved by the governing body, a formal amendment may be necessary.It is learnt that some shooters unhappy with their exclusion from the Asian Para Games squad refrained from approaching the courts for fear of being banned.Boccia dropped, contingent shrinks to 10 sportsThe controversy comes amid further reductions in India’s contingent for the Games. After para fencing, boccia has become the latest discipline to be dropped, with the sports ministry withholding clearance for the two-member team of Sachin Chamaria and Anjali Devi.India, initially scheduled to compete in 12 sports, will now participate in 10. The ministry cleared 166 athletes late Monday evening, taking the delegation’s strength to 275, including 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff. The Games begin in Nagoya on Oct 18.Para athletics accounts for the largest share of the contingent, with 62 athletes, including 46 men, along with 36 support staff.Para shooting chief coach JP Nautiyal has not received clearance despite representations from nine of the 13 selected shooters. Jeevan L Rai and Rakesh Singh will oversee the team. Nautiyal has faced allegations of violating selection criteria and demanding kickbacks.Cyclists’ hopes end with DRMThe final Delegation Registration Meeting (DRM) in Nagoya on Monday has effectively closed the door on additional entries. Para cyclists awaiting court relief against their exclusion will miss the Games even if they secure a favourable order later.Only Arshad Shaik will compete, while six other cyclists selected by the Cycling Federation of India and the PCI were omitted for allegedly failing to meet the prescribed criteria.Baretha questions Suhas’ inclusionPara badminton player Chirag Baretha has questioned the last-minute inclusion of LY Suhas, citing his absence from national and international competition since the Paris Paralympics in 2024.Baretha, a two-time Asian Para Games medallist, was excluded after the ministry ruled that he did not meet the selection criteria.“How a player can be qualified and sanctioned in the events at the Asian Para Games, he has never played a single game in the events he is qualified. Arbitration in sports can be visibly seen with the sanction issued for upcoming Games,” Baretha wrote on X.Manisha Patel, Shashank Kumar, Ammu Beulah Mohan and Rachna Patel were also denied clearance by the ministry.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Postseason Peralta Lifts Rays Past Guardians: 3 Takeaways From ALCS Game 2
articles.summary: The Rays defeated the Guardians, 3-0, on Tuesday night at Tropicana Field on the strength of their pitching and usual basepath pressure.
articles.body: TROPICANA FIELD (St. Petersburg, Fla.) — Game 2 of the ALCS was simple for the Rays. Just win. After watching a two-run lead slip away in Monday’s series opener, the last thing Tampa Bay wanted was to fall further behind against the Guardians and leave their home turf in a serious deficit. So all they had to do was respond. Rays manager Kevin Cash liked the way his players walked into the ballpark on Tuesday after suffering a deflating loss. He thought they were in a good headspace to even the series, reset the matchup, and regain their confidence. So they did. The Rays defeated the Guardians, 3-1, on Tuesday night at Tropicana Field on the strength of their pitching and usual basepath pressure. Here are my takeaways: 1. Ramirez’s Double-Gaffe Changed Everything The Rays are always creating pressure on the basepaths. They’re adept at spotting weaknesses in their opposition and exposing those flaws. And yet, even the Rays had to be surprised at the Guardians player who made not one, but two eyebrow-raising mistakes in a pivotal fourth inning. Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez forgot to cover the bag in one play. In another, he committed a fielding error when he couldn’t corral a ground ball that was hit to the hot corner. Both were plays he has completed an untold amount of times across his 14-year career. Both plays opened the door for the Rays to score multiple runs. The first Ramirez gaffe came on a Chandler Simpson groundball to short. Guardians shortstop Brayan Rocchio was never going to get the speedy Simpson out at first base. Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr., who was on base with a forceout, seemed to know that, or he was happy to keep sprinting either way, since there were two outs in the fourth inning at that point. As Mesa rounded second base and Simpson was called safe at first, Ramirez wasn’t covering third. Mesa didn’t hesitate, making it to third – standing up. That put runners on the corners for Rays second baseman Ben Williamson, with Guardians talented rookie southpaw Parker Messick on the mound in a scoreless game. Messick needed just one more out to get out of the inning unscathed. He thought he had that out when Williamson lined a routine chopper to third base that should’ve been vacuumed by Ramirez. Instead, it went between Ramirez’s legs and into left field, easily scoring Mesa from third. The Rays continued to capitalize. Catcher Liam Hicks roped a two-run single to center field to clear the bases and give Tampa Bay a 3-0 lead. All three runs were unearned. Who would’ve guessed, after all the positive impacts Ramirez has made for Cleveland, that the Rays’ big fourth-inning rally would be sparked by the unlikeliest player? 2. Fastball Freddy Was Perfect Right-hander Freddy Peralta watched Rays center fielder Johnny DeLuca secure a fly out for the final out of the fifth inning. Then he turned toward the Rays dugout and let out a primal scream. He was fired up. Typically, that’s the ceiling for Peralta, earning him the social-media nickname, "Five-Inning Freddy." But he had more heat left in the tank. With the Rays leading 3-0, manager Kevin Cash sent him back out for the sixth. Peralta stepped up to pitch his only clean inning of the night, retiring Nathaniel Lowe, Travis Bazzana and Petey Halpin in order to end his terrific outing on the highest of notes. Across eight career postseason starts, Tuesday night was the first time Peralta completed six innings in the playoffs. He relied on his high heater and his adjusted mechanics, including pitching from the stretch, to get him there. The Rays have trusted the veteran from the moment the Mets traded him to Tampa Bay this summer. In the regular season, he already showed them why they can continue to put their faith in him as their No. 2 starter behind ace Drew Rasmussen. But continuing to perform in October, on the sport’s grandest stage, under megawatt lights? That’s a different animal. 3. The Rays Finally Used Their Best Bullpen Arms Cash was under fire on Monday after failing to use his usual high-leverage relievers in lieu of going to his middle- to low-leverage arms in the Rays’ 7-3 loss to the Guardians in Game 1 of the ALCS. Tampa Bay’s longtime skipper made a series of questionable moves in that seemingly avoidable defeat, and he was sure to avoid any mistakes in Game 2, particularly when it came to the bullpen. Left-hander Ian Seymour, who has been a Swiss Army knife for the Rays this season, pitched 1 ⅓ scoreless innings from the final out of the seventh to the end of the eighth. He allowed just one hit and struck out two batters in that span, setting up the stage for Rays closer Bryan Baker to come in and do what he does best. Baker needed just eight pitches to take care of business in the top of the ninth inning. In the end, it was an easy win for the Rays. And those don’t come around often in October. 3 ½. What’s next? With the series even at one game apiece, neither team has announced their starting pitchers for what promises to be a crucial and intense Game 3. The ALCS will shift to Progressive Field in Cleveland for Games 3, 4 and 5. If needed, the series will return to Tropicana Field for Games 6 and 7.

articles.title: La policía caza un patinete eléctrico circulando a 88 km/h y esta es la multa que le cae a su dueño
articles.standfirst: Ha sucedido en San Andrés de Rabanedo (León), y el patinete, cuyo límite legal era de 25 km/h, había sido trucado
articles.summary: Ha sucedido en San Andrés de Rabanedo (León), y el patinete, cuyo límite legal era de 25 km/h, había sido trucado
articles.body: Desde el 1 de octubre, los usuarios de los patinetes eléctricos tienen que cumplir una serie de normas que antes no se les exigía. Así, estás obligados a llevar casco en las vías públicas, deben tener al menos 15 años, están obligados a contar con elementos reflectantes y deben tener su patinete asegurado, además de inscrito en un registro de la DGT. Para controlar todas estas nuevas medidas, los agentes de Tráfico y muchas policías locales están controlando de manera especial a los usuarios de estos vehículos, lo que incluye controles de alcohol y drogas, vigilancia para que no se empleen teléfonos ni auriculares mientras se conduce y sanciones cuando viajen dos personas en un mismo patinete. Pero los policías también pueden comprobar que el patinete no ha sido manipulado para superar el límite de 25 km/h. Y esto es lo que, según informa Europa Press, habría hecho el usuario de un patinete que la semana pasada fue denunciado por la policía local de San Andrés de Rabanedo (León), y que según el radar de velocidad circulaba a 88 km/h por las calles de la localidad. No han trascendido las circunstancias ni la edad del infractor o infractora, al que le ha caído una multa de 500 euros por trucar el patinete. Además, aunque tampoco este hecho se ha confirmado, la policía podría haber procedido a la inmovilización del patinete, su retirada inmediata y su traslado al depósito municipal, además abrir diligencias por un delito contra la seguridad vial por conducción temeraria.

articles.title: María Xiao y Álvaro Robles caen en octavos del Europeo y no podrán defender su oro
articles.standfirst: La pareja mixta española pierde en su segundo partido ante los alemanes Benedikt Duda y Nina Mittelham
articles.summary: La pareja mixta española pierde en su segundo partido ante los alemanes Benedikt Duda y Nina Mittelham
articles.body: La gran esperanza de medalla del tenis de mesa español en el Europeo de Liubliana (Eslovenia) no podrá esta vez repetir su histórico oro de 2024 en Linz (Austria). Álvaro Robles y María Xiao, vigentes campeones en la modalidad de dobles mixtos, se despidieron en los octavos de final tras caer por 0-3 (7-11, 8-11 y 8-11) ante los alemanes Benedikt Duda y Nina Mittelham. Robles y Xiao, que también lograron el primer diploma olímpico para el tenis de mesa español en París 2024, habían superado la criba inicial de dieciseisavos ante los ucranianos Andrii Grebeniuk y Anastasiya Dymytrenko, a los que vencieron por 3-1 (11-6, 11-4, 8-11 y 11-4). En esa misma ronda, Daniel y María Berzosa cedieron por 1-3 (3-11, 14-12, 7-11 y 5-11) ante los polacos Maciej Kubik y Natalia Bajor. En el individual femenino, Sofía-Xuan Zhang ganó por 3-1 (11-7, 13-15, 12-10 y 11-9) a la portuguesa Mariana Santa y María Berzosa venció por 3-1 (11-4, 11-5, 7-11 y 11-6) a la galesa Danielle Kelly. Por su parte, Elvira Rad perdió por 0-3 (6-11, 8-11 y 4-11) frente a la eslovena Ana Tofant. Zhang y Berzosa avanzan al cuadro principal, en el que ya esperaba la propia María Xiao, que a nivel individual defiende el bronce de hace dos años en Linz. En el individual masculino, Diego Lillo obtuvo un 3-0 frente al austríaco Andreas Levenko, con tres parciales de 11-0 registrados por la organización, mientras que Miguel Pantoja derrotó por 3-0 (11-4, 11-5 y 11-3) al groenlandés Poul Petersen. Además, Juan Pérez cayó por 0-3 (9-11, 9-11 y 5-11) ante el noruego Martin Froseth y Daniel Berzosa perdió por 2-3 (11-9, 11-9, 5-11, 4-11 y 6-11) frente al ruso Evgeny Tikhonov. Lillo continuará en el cuadro principal junto a Álvaro Robles. Sofía-Xuan Zhang y Elvira Rad accedieron ayer a los octavos de final del dobles femenino tras imponerse por 3-2 (11-6, 12-10, 7-11, 7-11 y 11-6) a las turcas Sibel Altinkaya y Ece Harac. Esta misma mañana, la pareja española se despedía del torneo tras caer por 1-3 (9-11, 11-7, 1-11 y 10-12) ante la eslovaca Tatiana Kukulkova y la polaca Natalia Bajor. La otra pareja con representación española, formada por María Berzosa y la moldava Alexandra Chiriacova, perdió ayer por 1-3 (8-11, 3-11, 12-10 y 4-11) frente a las rumanas Andreea Dragoman y Adina Diaconu. En el dobles masculino, Diego Lillo y Rafael de las Heras fueron superados por los suecos Anton Källberg y Kristian Karlsson por 1-3 (5-11, 4-11, 15-13 y 9-11) mientras que Juan Pérez y Daniel Berzosa cedieron por 2-3 (7-11, 9-11, 11-8, 11-6 y 5-11) ante el checo Stepan Brhel y el croata Leon Benko. Ambos encuentros correspondieron a los dieciseisavos de final del cuadro principal.

articles.title: Ranking the 6 Biggest Threats to Roman Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship in WWE
articles.summary: Roman Reigns has been booked so strongly during his latest run as WWE heavyweight champion that it's hard to imagine almost anyone on the active roster eventually dethroning him for the title.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns has been booked so strongly during his latest run as WWE heavyweight champion that it's hard to imagine almost anyone on the active roster eventually dethroning him for the title.

The Tribal Chief last reigned as world champion for nearly four years, and it took an army for Cody Rhodes to take that title from him at WrestleMania 40. This time around, Reigns is rewriting history by winning matches on his own and conquering all of the opponents he previously needed help to beat.

Following his successful defense against LA Knight at Money in the Bank, fans are looking ahead to who could be next to step up for a shot at the prestigious prize, even with Reigns focused on battling Sami Zayn for the Men's Crown Jewel Championship at Crown Jewel on November 7.

In the meantime, expect to see several Superstars stake their claim at a championship opportunity. More dominant than ever before, Reigns won't be going down without being pushed to his absolute limit and put down decisively.

From Penta lurking in the shadows with his newly won Money in the Bank briefcase to Oba Femi continuing to call him out, these are the six biggest threats to Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship.

Drew McIntyre is currently out of sight, out of mind in WWE, but he can't be counted out completely as a potential threat to Reigns and the World Heavyweight Championship he once held—albeit for five minutes.

Of course, the two of them have no shortage of history with each other. Their rivalry includes matches at WrestleMania 35, Survivor Series 2020 and Clash at the Castle 2022.

Reigns won every encounter, and in the latter two contests, the rest of The Bloodline got involved to ensure The Tribal Chief had his hand raised in victory. McIntyre hasn't forgotten about those shortcomings, going so far as to deem himself "The Bloodline Hunter" in early 2025.

Although the Scot managed to exact revenge on The Usos, he never got his rematch with Reigns. That could be coming now that Reigns is world heavyweight champ and many of his old rivalries are being revisited.

The Scottish Warrior hasn't been seen on WWE TV since WrestleMania 42, but he could reemerge at any moment, and when he does, there is a slight chance of him finally getting that elusive win over his archrival.

Despite experiencing a slow start in WWE, Royce Keys has amounted to main event stardom relatively quickly.

He made a memorable debut in the men's Royal Rumble match, won the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal, emerged victorious in six-man tag team action at SummerSlam and is now running rampant on Raw as the leader of The 946.

The formidable faction laid waste to The Usos and Solo Sikoa on Monday's Raw and has consistently been presented as a legitimate threat since arriving on Raw at the end of August. All signs point to the group battling The Bloodline in WarGames at Survivor Series—and ideally winning.

The finish should see Keys pin Reigns to earn an opportunity at the World Heavyweight Championship at the Royal Rumble. On paper, Keys may appear to be a filler opponent for The OTC ahead of WrestleMania 43, but what if WWE capitalized on his hot momentum by having him walk away with the gold, even if the reign was brief?

Keys has had serious singles potential since his days in All Elite Wrestling. At the rate The 946 is taking over Monday nights, he just might fulfill his destiny by becoming champ sooner rather than later.

It's no secret that Bron Breakker has had an underwhelming 2026, especially coming off his electric end to 2025 where he betrayed Seth Rollins and pinned CM Punk to win WarGames.

Nonetheless, he'll be wearing world title gold before long, as it's more a matter of when and not if. He just failed to win the men's Money in the Bank ladder match but could certainly be contending for the World Heavyweight Championship again by the beginning of 2027.

Although Reigns spent much of last year feuding with The Vision, he never actually squared off with Breakker one-on-one. WWE wisely held off on that first-ever encounter, and when it does finally happen, a world title should be up for grabs.

Reigns vs. Breakker could just as easily headline a WrestleMania, so there is the possibility of WWE going with that as one of next year's main events over Reigns vs. Oba Femi. That would serve as the perfect crowning moment for Breakker and put him back on the right path.

The company could do something drastic by having Breakker take the title from Reigns at the Royal Rumble and having him defend it against Femi at 'Mania instead, but The OTC being left out of that Night 2 main event simply doesn't seem to be in the cards.

Matches We Need After Money in the Bank 🏦

Penta winning a No. 1 contender's tournament and challenging Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship on Raw in Mexico City didn't appear to be anything other than a fun side quest for the masked marvel.

However, the stellar showing he had on that night convinced the powers that be at WWE that Penta did indeed belong among the elite toward the top of the card. Less than a month later, he won the men's Money in the Bank briefcase, guaranteeing him a future title shot at any time of his choosing.

Penta established not long after he lost to Reigns that he wanted a rematch, and with the contract now in his possession, he can get that rematch with Reigns whenever he wants. He can announce his title shot ahead of time or decide to cash it in on a whim and dethrone him for the belt that way.

It's strongly assumed Reigns will walk into WrestleMania as the world heavyweight champion, but Penta being Mr. Money in the Bank could derail those plans. The Tribal Chief can't rest easy knowing Penta is watching his every move and is ready to strike when he least expects it.

Penta may ultimately cash in on a SmackDown Superstar to capture the Undisputed WWE Championship, but his unfinished business with Reigns makes targeting The Tribal Chief particularly enticing.

Reigns was one day into his run as world heavyweight champion when he was confronted by Jacob Fatu and challenged to a match at Backlash.

The OTC barely came out on top in that outing, as well as in their Tribal Combat rematch at Clash in Italy.

Fatu's loss in the latter bout resulted in him having to "fall in line" and acknowledge Reigns by becoming a member of The Bloodline again. He's cooled off considerably since then, but he does remain an integral part of the main event picture on Raw by virtue of the group's ongoing rivalry with The 946.

Enough tension has been teased between Reigns and Fatu in recent months that a third match feels inevitable, specifically once Fatu is ready to break away from the rest of the group.

Reigns' poor treatment of The Samoan Werewolf should culminate in Fatu snapping on him once and for all and fighting him for the World Heavyweight Championship.

This could happen en route to WrestleMania 43, if not at the event itself with the big payoff being that Fatu is the one to ultimately unseat Reigns as champion. Their story will have come full circle in that case, cementing Fatu's status as a main event fixture.

Fatu won't be taking abuse from Reigns for much longer, and when he sets his sights back on the belt, The Tribal Chief better be ready.

Oba Femi was a threat to every top title in WWE the moment he debuted on the main roster in the Royal Rumble at the onset of 2026.

He was clearly coming for the championship in the wake of his WrestleMania win over Brock Lesnar, but Lesnar returning from his "retirement" to target Femi and avenge that loss at Clash in Italy put those aspirations on pause.

Femi reigned supreme in the King of the Ring tournament but decided to forgo the guaranteed title shot so he could face Lesnar inside Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam.

His destruction of The Beast Incarnate at the event was impressive, but it didn't explain why he opted to put the World Heavyweight Championship on the back-burner.

Even now, there's nothing holding him back from going after the gold other than the booking. He knocked off Bronson Reed at Money in the Bank and is once again stuck in limbo until it's time for him and Reigns to wage war over the world heavyweight title.

Reigns vs. Femi feels like a lock for WrestleMania 43, but The Ruler fulfilling his full potential by procuring the prestigious prize isn't set in stone. Reigns could find a way to win so WWE can create more adversity for Femi to overcome, but there really is no reason to delay something that should have already happened.

This will be a massive matchup once it comes to fruition, and although Reigns is in mild jeopardy of losing his coveted title before then, Femi has the greatest chance of seizing it from him.

articles.title: La campeona mundial de gimnasia artística no logra el visado de Países Bajos para defender su título
articles.standfirst: Angelina Melnikova, junto a otras dos gimnasta rusas, no podría defender en Rotterdam el oro en el concurso individual logrado el año pasado en Yakarta
articles.summary: Angelina Melnikova, junto a otras dos gimnasta rusas, no podría defender en Rotterdam el oro en el concurso individual logrado el año pasado en Yakarta
articles.body: Angelina Melnikova, vigente campeona del mundo del concurso completo y medalla de oro por equipos en los Juegos Olímpicos de Tokio 2020, junto a Anna Kalmykova y Viktoria Listunova, puede perderse el Mundial de Gimnasia Artística que se celebrará en la ciudad neerlandesa de Rotterdam. El gobierno de Países Bajos ha desestimado el visado de las tres gimnastas rusas y por tanto no cuentan, por ahora, con el documento imprescindible para ingresar en la nación donde se disputa la competición. La posible ausencia de la favorita y defensora del título, Angelina Melnikova, es lo que más preocupa a la Federación Rusa de Gimnasia, que ya está en conversaciones con el Comité Olímpico Internacional (COI), para intentar resolver la situación, tanto de las gimnastas, como de otras deportistas del país. El Mundial reparte las primeras plazas de clasificación para los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028. La deportista rusa ha mostrado su enfado por su visa holandesa denegada: "Entiendo que el deporte, hasta cierto punto, es político. Pero para mí, el deporte es la única plataforma, al menos por ahora, donde puedes ganar de manera completamente justa y nadie puede arrebatártelo, pero han encontrado una manera de hacerlo", declaró Angelina. "No es que solo estemos pidiendo ser incluidas en la competencia. Tenemos un lugar oficial que ganamos para el Campeonato Mundial y de alguna manera, te has ganado el derecho a estar allí, pero están creando obstáculos", cerró la gimnasta, campeona del concurso completo en Yakarta 2025, que este año también se proclamo campeona de Europa en Zagreb.

articles.summary: Jack Harvey has set his sights on the 2027 Indianapolis 500 despite announcing that he has been diagnosed with cancer.
articles.body: Jack Harvey has set his sights on the 2027 Indianapolis 500 despite announcing that he has been diagnosed with cancer. The 33-year-old British driver shared the news on Tuesday, October 13, in a statement that made clear he intends to keep working toward his racing plans. Harvey also hopes to be present for the IndyCar season opener in St. Petersburg in March, where he works as a FOX Sports pit reporter. He has not publicly identified the type of cancer, but said he is receiving excellent care and support as he faces the diagnosis.Jack Harvey keeps his 2027 IndyCar plans in viewJack Harvey’s statement linked the news to a career built around finding his next chance in motorsport. “My entire career has been about fighting for what’s next. The next opportunity. The next chance to prove myself. The next time I could get back in the car and show what I’m capable of.”He explained that progress had not always come in a straight line. “There have been moments when the path forward was obvious, and plenty when it wasn’t. I’ve had to earn opportunities, fight to keep them, and learn how to keep moving when things didn’t go the way I planned.”The diagnosis, he wrote, has brought a new challenge, but has not changed the targets he has set for next year. “Life has delivered a new fight to my doorstep. I have recently been diagnosed with cancer.”“My goals for 2027 have not changed. I plan to be on the grid in St. Pete and strapping back into a race car this May in preparation for the Indianapolis 500.”Harvey has raced in the Indy 500 for Dreyer & Reinbold Racing in each of the past two years, even as he took on broadcast work with FOX. His 2027 plan includes returning to the season opener in his reporting role and pursuing another chance to race at Indianapolis. articles.title: Man City’s appeal over 114 charges to be heard by January, regulator says
articles.summary: Manchester City have contested the guilty verdict, and the appeal will be heard by mid-January or the end of January.
articles.body:
Manchester City’s appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules is expected to be heard by January, according to the chair of English football’s independent regulator.

“The Premier League has said that they want to get this resolved within the season, and actually, of course, it’s not the Premier League, it’s an independent commission that’s actually going to hear this, made up of three retired judges or lawyers,” Independent Football Regulator (IFR) chair David Kogan told Times Radio on Wednesday.

“My understanding is that there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January,” he added.

“But as I say, it’s not our process, it’s that of the Premier League’s independent commission. What I don’t think we can do is take any judgment until we’re quite clear.”

City, who have repeatedly maintained they are innocent of any wrongdoing , are currently top of the Premier League table with six wins out of six following Sunday’s 3-0 defeat of Liverpool.

No sanction has been announced, but City could face a heavy points deduction leading to relegation. There has even been speculation they could be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won between 2009 and 2018.

IFR’s Kogan said on Tuesday he would resign if there was political interference in any future IFR investigations of City.

An independent commission found the club guilty on charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018. It had been accused of using ‘sham’ contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce reported costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.2 billion).

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for his initial comments on the case, saying he would be “really concerned” if City’s Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict.

Downing Street later had to backtrack, saying no one was “above the rules”.

Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy.

“We’ve had absolutely no interference from anybody since we created the regulator a year ago,” Kogan said. “We cannot, when regulating football, be subject to political interference on decisions we make about owners, directors or anything else.”

“And I won’t actually be prepared to run an organisation which is subject to that degree of interference,” he added.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said last week he “completely trusts” the club and believes it will win its appeal.

articles.title: Tennessee football announces uniform combination for Alabama game
articles.summary: Tennessee football and Alabama will both wear their traditional home uniforms for a special color-on-color matchup at Neyland Stadium on Oct. 17.
articles.body:
Tennessee football will wear orange jerseys as part part of a special technicolor uniform matchup with Alabama at Neyland Stadium.

The Vols will wear white helmets and pants and orange tops while Alabama wears crimson helmets and jerseys and white pants.

The orange and crimson uniforms are part of a two year agreement between both programs and the SEC to wear home uniforms for the Third Saturday in October in each of the next two seasons.

The No. 14 Vols (5-1, 2-1 SEC) host No. 7 Alabama (5-1, 2-1) at Neyland Stadium on Oct. 17 (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC).

What is Tennessee's record in each uniform combination during the 2026 season?

Tennessee is 2-1 in their traditional home uniforms of white helmets and pants, and orange jerseys so far this season. The Vols routed Furman 56-9 win in on Sept. 5 and beat Kennesaw State 42-9 on Sept. 19, both games at Neyland Stadium. They also suffered a 20-17 loss to No. 1 Texas on Sept. 26 while wearing the usual home uniform.

UT has worn white helmets, uniforms and pants twice this season and won both times, first at Georgia Tech on Sept. 12 and again on Oct. 10 at Arkansas . It won two of four games in the all-white combination in 2025, notching wins over Kentucky and Florida but losing to Alabama and Illinois.

The Vols are also a perfect 5-0 in grey uniforms since 2022, with the latest win coming on Oct. 3 at home vs. Auburn . They also beat LSU 40-13 in 2022, Austin Peay 30-13 in 2023, Chattanooga 69-3 in 2024 and New Mexico State 42-9 in 2025 while wearing different editions of the "Smokey Grey" uniforms.

What alternate uniforms will Tennessee wear this season?

The Vols wore alternate uniforms for the first time this season vs. Auburn, when they honored the iconic coach Gen. Robert Neyland with their grey "Neyland Legacy" uniforms .

The special, throwback flare Tennessee is bringing to the Third Saturday in October this year isn't necessarily an alternate uniform, but this year's game will be the first color-on-color clash between the two rivals since 1970.

The Vols also have their "dark mode" all black uniforms available for a later date. They are 5-2 when wearing black alternate uniforms since 2009. The last time UT wore black football uniforms, they lost 33-27 to Oklahoma at Neyland Stadium on Nov. 1, 2025.

articles.title: Wagner on "brutal blow" to Skhiri, Castro-Montes fit for Köln voyage to Frankfurt
articles.summary: As their build up to Friday's clash with Eintracht Frankfurt begins, René Wagner said the loss of Ellyes Skhiri is a difficult one to accept. “That's a bruta...
articles.body:
As their build up to Friday's clash with Eintracht Frankfurt begins, René Wagner said the loss of Ellyes Skhiri is a difficult one to accept.

"That's a brutal blow for us. I hope that Ellyes will be available again at the start of next year," he said in this afternoon's press conference.

"However, I don't want to give a precise prognosis. Tom Krauß came on at halftime in the derby and did well.

"We also have an option with Paul Okon-Engstler [as a replacement option]," he added, before discussing the full-back positions.

"Alessio Castro-Montes is an option for the squad again for Friday. It's a very tight race between Borna Sosa and Gideon Mensah.

"Both are doing well in training. After the derby win, Borna might have a slight edge right now, but that can change at any time," Wagner said.

Savouring the sweet taste of victory from last Sunday's Rhinederby, Wagner also praised his centre-half duo and encouraged Linton Maina.

"Jahmai and Locho as the center-back duo are finding their rhythm better and better and defended a lot against Gladbach.

They take steps forward in every game. But as a group, we want to keep stabilizing defensively. Linton needs to feel comfortable.

"He needs to sense the trust. We're giving him that feeling. He shows up with a lot of motivation in every training session.

Over the summer, he did a ton of sprints and is also defensively involved with a great deal of meticulousness," the 38-year-old concluded.

articles.title: Don Mattingly expected to return as Phillies manager
articles.summary: Don Mattingly will reportedly once again helm the team in 2027
articles.body:
If you were hoping for dramatic changes with the Phillies for the 2027 season, it looks like it isn't going to come in the form of a new manager. According to this story by Charlotte Varnes, the Phillies are planning to name Don Mattingly as the full-time manager:

Mattingly drew mixed reviews for his performance after taking over for Rob Thomson in late April. The team was largely successful, going 79-55 after his hire, earning the National League's final playoff spot before losing in the Wild Card round. But many of Mattingly's decisions came under scrutiny, particularly his handling of the bullpen. His overuse of key relievers, and his tendency to repeatedly warm up relievers, seemed to leave them badly worn out by the end of the season.

This move will not go over well with fans hoping to see dramatic changes after five years of playoff failures, but the looming threat of an extended lockout to start the 2027 season may have influenced the Phillies' decision. It is no secret they were interested in Alex Cora , but Cora announced his intention to take next year off. The Phillies likely felt that with the 2027 season likely to be delayed or shortened, it would make sense to maintain some sense of continuity and re-assess next year.

articles.title: Jets Kicking the Tires on 72 Career Sack Veteran Before Pats Game
articles.summary: The New York Jets are kicking the tires on a 72-career sack specialist before the New England Patriots game in Week 6. The post Jets Kicking the Tires on 72...
articles.body:
The New York Jets are doing their homework before the New England Patriots game in Week 6.

NFL Insider Tom Pelissero revealed on X that the Jets "worked out" veteran pass rusher Matthew Judon on Tuesday, October 13.

Judon, 34, entered the league in 2016 as the No. 146 overall pick in the fifth round. He spent the first five years of his career with the Baltimore Ravens before bouncing around the league. Most recently, Judon spent some time on the San Francisco 49ers' practice squad this season.

Judon has been named to four Pro Bowls. Across his 11 seasons at the NFL level, Judon has appeared in 146 games, and he has made 100 starts. With those opportunities, Judon has collected 72 sacks, nine forced fumbles, an interception that was returned to the house for a touchdown, 20 pass deflections, four fumble recoveries, 430 total tackles, 95 tackles for loss, and 177 quarterback hits.

At the time of publication, this was just a workout. However, if the Jets end up signing Judon, they will prove to be his final infinity stone in the AFC East.

Judon spent three seasons with the Patriots (2021-23), he was with the Miami Dolphins for five months in 2025, and finally he was with the Buffalo Bills for the final stretch of the 2025 campaign. If he were to sign with the Jets, Judon would have suited up for every team in the AFC East.

So this was an interesting workout for the Jets to kick the tires on.

In the 1999 movie Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me , Powers constantly asks Basil Exposition, "Whoop-de-doo! What does it all mean, Basil?"

We ask that question now. Why are the Jets working out Judon? Is this to add a quality pass rusher to their emergency list for the future? Does this suggest some injury news is coming for the green and white? What does it all mean?

There was plenty of speculation on social media.

"So, we are bound to get some negative injury news," analyst Paul Fiore responded.

"I don't think so, it's clear we need more pass rush juice . Never really replaced [Braiden] McGregor ," a Jets fan responded .

"We NEED better edge depth I'd like this, I wonder if this means a WMD trade is in the works," another Jets fan said.

"can't imagine why they would do that this week of all weeks……." Patriots analyst Sara Marshall wrote .

The Jets play the Patriots this week. She is suggesting that perhaps the sole reason the Jets were working out Judon is to gain information ahead of the matchup this weekend.

"If the Jets want information out of this workout, they're not going to get it. Judon has never played under Mike Vrabel or Zak Kuhr. Also, he has never played a game with Drake Maye . His only teammates that currently remain with the Patriots are Mike Onwenu (IR), Christian Barmore , Marcus Jones, Hunter Henry, Christian Gonzalez, DeMario Douglas, and Bryce Baringer (IR). (Technically, he was teammates with Drake Maye, Dell Pettus, and Christian Elliss, but never took a snap in a football game with any of them on the field.) The last time he took a snap for the Patriots was October 1, 2023," Patriots writer Theo Diesenhaus explained.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson gives credit to the Jets' defense after loss
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson gave the Jets defense their flowers.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns entered Sunday's road game against the New York Jets at 3-1, with the vibes being at an all-time high this season. The rain from Hurricane Isasis made conditions less than ideal, but it was the Jets' defense that really gave this Browns offense fits. This fact was something that quarterback Deshaun Watson acknowledged and spoke about.

Following Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets, Watson gave the Jets their flowers:

"You just got to give the Jets the credit. They did a good job of just showing different pressures and bringing it from all over the place."

A ton of credit is owed to Jets rookie pass rusher David Bailey. Bailey had his coming-out party against the Browns, finishing with three sacks on the day. As a whole, the Jets limited the Browns to just 198 yards of total offense, something they can not afford to repeat this Sunday as they play against the Baltimore Ravens .

articles.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic only has 2-word reaction to Los Angeles fan’s NSYNC dance
articles.summary: A viral fan caught the attention of Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic by dancing to a song by iconic boy band NSYNC during the team’s preseason game agains...
articles.body:
A viral fan caught the attention of Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic by dancing to a song by iconic boy band NSYNC during the team's preseason game against the Golden State Warriors .

Doncic sat out of the Lakers' game against the Warriors. That doesn't mean he didn't enjoy the game, though, as he was taking in the sights during the first quarter break.

He spotted a fan dancing to NSYNC. The fan was wearing his jersey, and Doncic acknowledged him and appeared to say , "He's good," after watching the fan's moves.

Why did Luka Doncic miss the Lakers' preseason game against the Warriors?

After sitting out last week's preseason game against the Warriors, Doncic did the same on Tuesday, Oct. 13 . He is still recovering from a hamstring injury that affected him in the playoffs.

While he has looked good in limited preseason action, Lakers coach JJ Reddick opted to have him sit out of the latest Warriors clash, noting that there was "no injury" to be concerned about.

The Lakers have one more preseason game against the Denver Nuggets before opening the regular season against the Warriors on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

You could argue that Doncic is coming off the best season of his career. He played in 64 games and started all of them during the 2025-26 regular season. He averaged 33.5 points per game, his highest mark since the 2023-24 season with the Dallas Mavericks. Additionally, he averaged 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists per game.

He is now the unquestioned leader of the Lakers with LeBron James' departure. The Lakers are hoping to make it past the Western Conference Semifinals in 2026. They narrowly survived the Houston Rockets after almost blowing a 3-0 series lead. They were then swept by the then-reigning NBA champions, the Oklahoma City Thunder.
