articles.title: Know Your Enemy: A Conversation with the Washington Huskies Dawg Pound
articles.summary: This week I was lucky enough to exchange questions with Mark Shafer from the Dawg Pound about Friday’s game between the Huskers and the Boilermakers. Coach F...
articles.body:
This week I was lucky enough to exchange questions with Mark Shafer from the Dawg Pound about Friday's game between the Huskers and the Boilermakers.

Coach Fisch said today he'd be surprised if starting QB Demond Williams was able to play on Friday. What can you tell us about backup QB Elijah Brown?

Elijah Brown is an experienced backup, having spent the previous 2 seasons at Stanford, throwing for 829 yards, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in 2025 for the Cardinal, leading them to a win over rival California. In the preseason, he was described as an old veteran, without Williams' athletic ability. Against Iowa after Williams' injury, it was a breath of fresh air, as Brown made decisive reads, getting the ball out quickly to his receivers like a point guard on the basketball court. All told, he went 28-39 for 251 yards and 3 touchdowns, which is not bad for a backup. However, it was during a blowout and Iowa was probably playing soft coverages, or they didn't have film on him. But, if he can continue that momentum, maybe a distributor can wake up a previously stuck offense.

Purdue's trading of Ryan Walters to Washington for cash considerations and a player to be named later sure looks like a good deal for Purdue at this moment. What are Washington fans feelings about Walters?

I think that for me personally, I could excuse a bumpy year one as Walters implementing his system to his liking. The Huskies got some key pieces back, like safety Alex McLaughlin, their leading tackler, and the previously electric Zaydrius Rainey-Sale at linebacker. Additionally, young Freshmen like Jeron Jones at corner and Derek Colman-Brusa at defensive tackle were to catapult this unit into the upper echelon in the country. Now, I wouldn't be surprised if they end up near the bottom. Missed tackles, miscommunication and penalties aplenty have marred Walters' second year and made me (and a lot of other Husky fans) sour on him. I get that the Huskies lost to Iowa, but it looked like these Dawgs just rolled over and got willingly stomped on by a Hawkeye team just…doing what they do, and have done for about 40 years. I wanted to like this hire, I really did. But if anything it shows the Huskies lack discipline, and are fundamentally unsound. They can't get any push up front either, as they gave up 263 yards rushing, and sit in the bottom half of the country in sacks with 10. Overall, the Walters Experiment has to this point been a failure, and Devon Witherspoon's not walking through that door, so unfortunately, unless this team turns around fast, they'll continue to be outworked by the more cohesive units in the Big Ten.

This will be Washington's first game not on the West Coast, how much of a factor do you think that will be on Friday?

Fisch is infamous for his road record outside of the Pacific Time Zone (standing at 1-6, the only win coming on a furious 4 th quarter comeback against Maryland in 2025). Every time the Dawgs travel eastward, it's a case of them not being awake to start the game, or not being able to overcome the weather or getting out-physicaled, or sometimes all 3. Granted, the talent level probably wasn't where it should've been, but they got outplayed and out-hustled by Wisconsin last year, who finished 4-8.

As for Friday night, I expect more of the same: relative lethargy to start out, maybe making it a better game in the second half. With a new quarterback, maybe they'll surprise me, but I don't see a path to victory right now.

Brian Bonner Jr. gets the bulk of carries for the Huskies, but hasn't had a touchdown yet this season, with Williams out will he be expected to carry more of the load?

Seeing as how Brown is not the mobile athlete that Williams is, I'd expect to see a steady diet of Brian Bonner, as the running back room is down the top 2 guys (Quaid Carr and Oregon transfer Jayden Limar) because of season ending injuries to both. Bonner is a great athlete, with good burst, but he's a Freshman, and as such, his vision needs work. During the game against USC, Fisch attempted to alleviate that by running a lot of gap runs (as opposed to the zone that he likes to run). Bonner responded with 89 yards in his best performance as a Husky yet. I think if Fisch plays to Bonner's strength, maybe he could get across the goal line in this game?

Looking at the defensive side of the ball, which units are the strengths and which are the weaknesses?

The strengths are definitely the secondary and linebackers. Alex McLaughlin once again leads the team in tackles with 44, with senior linebacker Jacob Manu trailing behind him with 35. McLaughlin also has 2 interceptions and 1 forced fumble. Not to be outdone, Zaydrius Rainey Sale and Xe'ree Alexander have 25 and 22 tackles, respectively. The weaknesses are on the defensive line, and the other corners, as they both haven't lived up to their preseason hype. The Huskies can't get any push up front, and they routinely played out of position against Iowa, giving up over 200 passing yards and 200 rushing yards. I don't know what can be done to fix that, save for firing Walters, but something must be done!

Washington slings the ball around to a lot of different guys with 8 having at least one touchdown. Is WR depth the strength of this offense?

I'd say that this room is long on depth, short on experience. Yes, there's a lot of exciting young talent in Dezmen Roebuck (the team's leading pass catcher, with 43 receptions for 387 yards), and Chris Lawson (second behind Roebuck). But on tape, you see it plainly, they can't get a whole lot of separation, and that won't net you a lot of yards, obviously. To that end, Fisch has modified his offense a bit, mixing in more bubble screens to Roebuck, for example. But it hasn't produced the explosive results a lot of UW fans were promised, and maybe that starts with the quarterback. Demond Williams has regressed and now seems less confident, less willing to get the ball out quickly, and that has limited these receivers a bit, I think. With Brown in line to start, maybe that stirs the receivers up and unlocks something in this offense.

What's your prediction for Friday night's game?

There are a lot of factors working against the Huskies: most likely starting QB2, going all the way to Indiana from Washington, facing a team no doubt looking to carry their momentum from a thrashing of Minnesota forward. That, combined with their struggles, leaves me with little hope for a Husky victory. I was surprised at Brown's performance last Friday night, however, so I hope that I can be pleasantly surprised once again, this time with a victory. But in a battle between struggle spots and bright spots, I think the struggle spots are going to win out, and the Huskies will further sink down in the mire of something worse than mediocrity.

articles.title: Is the rebuild over? Dybantsa, Young and Davis give Washington an interesting core -- for now
articles.summary: Washington WizardsLast season: 17-65, missed playoffs.COACH: Brian Keefe (fourth season, 43-160).
articles.body:
COACH: Brian Keefe (fourth season, 43-160).

DEPARTURES: G D'Angelo Russell, F Julian Reese, F Cam Whitmore.

ADDITIONS: F AJ Dybantsa, C Deandre Ayton, G Tre Mann.

After three straight seasons with under 19 wins, the Wizards finally caught a break when they won the draft lottery and the right to take Dybantsa. Even before that, Washington was making bold moves, acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis in trades last season. Young barely played for the Wizards and Davis didn't at all, but they're now healthy and ready for the start of the season. At the very least, those two can take some pressure off Dybantsa and other youngsters like Alex Sarr and Bub Carrington.

The good: It's certainly possible that a change of scenery is just what Young needed. On the offensive end, he can be an elite playmaker that opponents must account for, and if he clicks with Davis, Washington could improve significantly. Davis has the potential to revitalize the Wizards at the defensive end, and Dybantsa could be the franchise player Washington has been waiting to acquire for years.

The not-so-good: Davis can become a free agent after this season, and if he's not interested in staying, the Wizards might end up having to trade him before too long. Young, on the other hand, was signed to a four-year, $212 million extension after playing only five games in a Washington uniform. So the Wizards are committed to him for better or worse. It's a roster that's interesting, but there's no way of knowing how well the fit will end up being — and for how long.

Dybantsa's development is the most important issue for the Wizards, but the most pressing question from a league-wide perspective is whether Davis can play like a superstar at age 33. If so, Washington could make a climb in the standings — or Davis could become a major trade target for a contender.

Meanwhile, the Wizards traded for Ayton in the offseason. He's a decent insurance policy in case Davis' tenure in Washington is a short one, but if everyone is healthy, the Wizards suddenly have some impressive size with the 7-foot Ayton, 7-foot Sarr and 6-foot-10 Davis.

articles.title: Is Dave Roberts going to bench Shohei Ohtani in the NLCS?
articles.summary: The Dodgers tend to rile up a lot of emotions in almost every baseball fan. But that might apply to Red Sox fans more than most. That’s primarily due to two...
articles.body:
The Dodgers tend to rile up a lot of emotions in almost every baseball fan. But that might apply to Red Sox fans more than most. That's primarily due to two people, both of whom happen to be two of the most important people in Red Sox history: Mookie Betts and Dave Roberts.

Is Dave Roberts still more famous for the steal in 2004 than for anything he's done in the LA dugout? That probably depends on who you ask. And while it's obviously impossible for me to answer that objectively — my perspective of his career and fame is totally colored by my Red Sox fandom — I think the answer is yes. His stolen base in Game 4 is probably the most important steal in baseball history. Your grandkids are going to know about it. If a prominent media outlet put it on a list of the 10 biggest moments in MLB history, I don't think many people would object. I can't even really think of any other stolen base that's anywhere near as famous, with the possible exception of Jackie Robinson's steal of home in the 1955 World Series, which happened in a game that the Dodgers didn't even win.

When you're responsible for one of the biggest moments in baseball history, that's going to be what you're remembered for, no matter how successful of a managerial career you subsequently have. And that's particularly true in baseball, where coaches aren't as consequential as they are in other sports and don't build up personality cults.

But it's quite possible that Roberts is about to do something that may one day come to rival the steal in terms of its historical half-life: He may bench the greatest baseball player of all-time in the playoffs.

It has been a weird year for Shohei Ohtani. 2026 was supposed to be the year he returned to pitching and hitting full-time and, for a while there, things were looking great. He started 14 games over the first three months of the season, posting an outstanding 2.87 ERA and looking poised to compete for his first Cy Young Award. And with 18 homers and an OPS over .900 through the first half of the season, it wasn't hard to imagine him winning both the MVP and the Cy Young in what would probably be the greatest single season by any professional athlete in world sports history.

Unfortunately, a knee injury cut his pitching season short. A subsequent right biceps strain has put a serious damper on his hitting. Still struggling with both injuries, Ohtani went on the IL in late September amidst one of the worst slumps of his career. There were even doubts about whether he would be able to play in the postseason. Ohtani still ended up being incredibly valuable to the Dodgers, leading the team in bWAR. He also made it back for the playoffs. But it's been ugly, as he is just 3-20 without a single extrabase hit.

Shohei Ohtani is not currently Shohei Ohtani. The best player in the game is hurting his team. Roberts has already moved him down the order, and now we know that the Dodgers have discussed taking him out of the lineup altogether.

For tonight, anyway, Roberts is not going to push that detonator. "He's adamant he feels good enough to be in there. He's close to finding something with his swing. I feel great about it," Roberts said. "He was very convicted that he is onto something mechanically. He was adamant that he can help us. He's well enough to help us win a baseball game. So that's all I needed to hear."

From the moment he established himself as a star the likes of which the sport has never before seen, it's been clear that Shohei Ohtani — not Dave Roberts or Joe Madden or Phil Nevin — decides when and where Shohei Ohtani plays. So Roberts' quote isn't all that surprising. But if what if the mechanical tweaks don't work? What if we see another 0-fer tonight filled with noncompetitive at-bats? What if the Dodgers lose, and Dave Roberts is, once again, forced to try to save a team down three games to none in the league championship series?

Tomorrow night, Roberts might face what would be a legacy-defining moment for most managers. Fortunately for him he's been there before.

Use this space to talk about Roberts, Ohtani, and whatever else you want and, as always, be good to one another.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Week 6: TE Edition
articles.summary: Entering Week 6, here are three unconventional recommended TE bargains to start, as well as three supposedly must-start TEs to sit.
articles.body:
If you are desperate for TE production and don't have a consensus top-12 Week 5 fantasy tight end, here are three highly unconventional, solid-upside bargains. Also, if you're planning to start one of those previously referenced top-12 fantasy TEs , these three are riskier than usual. As always, let's use FantasyPros' Week 5 composite rankings as our guide.

Start - Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (Ranked 16th)

With Terrance Ferguson still on injured reserve, longtime Ram Tyler Higbee has stepped up, generally operating as Matthew Stafford's #2 or #3 receiving option. He'll turn 34 on New Year's Day, but age doesn't seem to matter for Higbee, who's playing his best football in years. A matchup against the Cardinals should keep him rolling.

Start - Kyle Pitts, Atlanta Falcons (Ranked 21st)

How far has Kyle Pitts' stock plummeted? Last year's overall TE2 is now outside the top 30, and his Week 6 rank suggests he's completely unstartable in fantasy. But Pitts won't be a season-long bust -- not to the degree we've seen so far. He has enough double-digit potential to warrant a strong dart throw.

Start - Colston Loveland, Chicago Bears (Ranked 15th)

Colston Loveland has scored 2.9 fewer fantasy points than Pitts. A similarly high-priced former first-round pick, Loveland is on pace for a 44-374-0 receiving line. In other words, things will balance out, and you don't want him on your bench when they do.

Sit - Dalton Kincaid, Buffalo Bills (Ranked 8th)

He was recommended as a sit last week because of a tough matchup against the Rams. I expect the Raiders to move the ball better this week than we've seen recently, keeping the ball out of Josh Allen's hands more than usual. Kincaid might get fewer than five looks. Given his Week 6 rankings, I'd call him a fade.

Sit - Harold Fannin Jr., Cleveland Browns (Ranked 10th)

I wasn't sold on Harold Fannin Jr. this preseason, and I wasn't sold on him even after his strong start. He usually won't get enough targets to stay in the top 10 unless he scores, and in this offense, scoring is a big weekly question mark.

Sit - Trey McBride, Arizona Cardinals (Ranked 3rd)

No way! Well, here's what we know. McBride isn't always a fantasy starter, scoring in single digits four times in 2024 and once last year. The opposing Rams have locked down prolific passing attacks. McBride probably will end up with around six catches for 37 yards on 11 targets. If you're happy with that, go for it. If not, then stun your friends and family and bench McBride.

articles.title: 2026 Yankees Team MVP: Cam Schlittler
articles.summary: I thought 2025’s rookie sensation would be good. I didn’t expect this
articles.body:
We close a bit of a circle with this post, as I was fortunate to write Cam Schlittler's season preview post all the way back in March. This was how good(ish) FanGraphs thought he would be:

Of course Cam ended the year with a 1.95 ERA, 2.56 FIP, 31 percent strikeout rate, 6.4 percent walk rate, and 6.2 fWAR. It is hard to think in recent seasons of a player so dramatically outplaying their Depth Chart projections, so much so that said player went from a projected third-ish pitcher in a rotation to the likely Cy Young winner. That was Cam Schlittler's 2026, and its why he's not just the Yankees' MVP, but he'll likely get his share of AL MVP votes overall.

This is the ninth-most-valuable season, by fWAR, for the Yankees since 1920, along with the third-lowest ERA and fifth-lowest FIP. Perhaps more to the point is the per-inning effectiveness of Cam; nobody throws 270 innings anymore:

When you adjust for the fact that Cam has to play under the constraints of baseball in 2026, you can make a good argument he just put up the second-best pitching season in the history of the organization. Gator in '78 has always been the gold standard for pitching in pinstripes, but he has some company atop the best single-seasons we've ever seen from a Yankee hurler.

We need to take a moment and acknowledge Ben Rice, who for so many stretches of the season, including the disastrous ALDS loss to the Rays, was the only batter who seemed interested in doing damage. In a year with so little Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton, those 41 home runs and a 149 wRC+ proved that Rice isn't just a Major League regular but a new foundation for the franchise moving forward. He is comfortably the runner up in this race, the Robin to Cam's Batman as the Massachusetts boys virtually dragged the Yankees themselves into the AL playoff picture.

Ben was of particular import because of how weak the lineup was otherwise, whereas Cam was the first among an excellent group, a starting rotation that was the best in baseball and a bullpen unit that was the second best. Still, having such a good season that you rocket yourself past name brands like Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón gets you the hardware.

So what comes next for the Yankees' MVP?

There will be the formal stuff, the MLB Awards will be announced and he will likely be consecrated as the deserved Cy Young winner. There was some rumbling down the stretch that Schlittler should get serious MVP consideration, with both Junior Caminero and Yordan Alvarez having holes in their cases, and Bobby Witt Jr. toiling away in personal excellence and seeming anonymity in Kansas City. I think Cam will fall just a bit short in that race, but the fact we can discuss it at all speaks to the quality of his season.

Headed into 2027 Schlittler is the unquestioned ace of the staff, a staff that should once again be a strength of the ball club — his youth also makes me perhaps irrationally optimistic he can "ramp up" in a shortened Spring Training faster than some of the veterans in the rotation. I worry that we're going to develop a little bit of Aaron Judge-ness with him — we saw such a peak, it is quite unlikely he ever has a sub-2.00 ERA season again. A 2.50 ERA would be a notable step back from what Cam did this year, and yet would have him be fifth in all of baseball this year, he was that good.

The biggest question mark we have is how Cam can adjust with a full offseason. The defining feature of his 2026 was how he was able to adjust from start to start, after that strange four-homer start against Detroit to close June he allowed just six long balls over the remaining 15 outings of the regular season. He walked five Boston batters in August, then seven total in his last five starts. He had those same Red Sox geared up for his fastball-heavy approach to open the Wild Card Series, and then dropped curveballs on Boston's lineup and watched them flail around.

These kind of adjustments, the education of an ace on the fly, are what makes me so grateful to have had this season from Cam, and so excited to see where he goes. With his combination of age, stuff, approach and attitude, the sky's the limit for the AL's best pitcher, and the Yankees' MVP.

articles.title: DeLorean Signs Up for Flying Car Racing Without Showing a Flying Car, a Pilot or a Race Date
articles.summary: DeLorean Motor Company is now a flying car constructor, according to DeLorean Motor Company. It announced on October 13 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Fra...
articles.body:
DeLorean Motor Company is now a flying car constructor, according to DeLorean Motor Company. It announced on October 13 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco that it will enter the Airspeeder International Series, an electric flying car racing series, as constructor of the United States team. The squad is called the DeLorean Airspeeder Team and is due to debut when the 2026–27 season opens in November.

The announcement, distributed with a set of press images, calls DeLorean the first American constructor in flying car racing. It gives no date or venue for that November opener.

The aircraft design, pilot line-up and sporting program will be revealed "ahead of the season opener," the release says. Today the team has no named pilot and no shown aircraft. It does not say how many teams are on the grid. It refers to national teams "from around the world" without naming one, and the team's boilerplate lists "technology partners" without naming any. There is no budget, sponsor or funding source anywhere in the text.

The company description at the bottom talks about the DeLorean brand's legacy and does not mention a product the company currently builds.

In this series, national teams fly electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft through electronically defined courses in three dimensions instead of lapping a circuit. For its first season the DeLorean team will fly the Airspeeder Mk3C, with DeLorean "leading its design identity." The release never defines that phrase, and it does not say who builds, owns or maintains the aircraft.

The aircraft DeLorean designs for itself arrives a season later. The 2027–28 DeLorean Airspeeder is to be developed with student engineering teams at US universities, a list that names the University of California, UC Berkeley and Georgia Tech in one sentence without saying how many partners that is, which campuses are involved or what the students will be asked to do.

Chief Brand Officer Cameron Wynne said "People have pictured a DeLorean in the sky for forty years." The only DeLorean that has flown so far is the one in the Back to the Future films. Airspeeder founder and CEO Matt Pearson called DeLorean the original flying car brand.

Wynne's practical case is regulatory. DeLorean wants to help shape the safety and compliance frameworks that flying vehicles will need, and he described widespread use as still over the horizon. Plenty of programs in this space never leave the ground: Volkswagen's V.MO ended in 2024 after five years without carrying a paying passenger, as we covered .

Airspeeder and DeLorean say they will share more about the constructor relationship "in the coming months." The aircraft, pilots and sporting program are due before the November opener.

Does leading the design identity of someone else's aircraft earn DeLorean the title of constructor?

articles.title: 3 things from Ryan Day’s Week 7 presser
articles.summary: Ryan Day gave a few injury updates ahead of Ohio State’s battle with Indiana, discussed the Buckeyes’ red zone offense and more in his weekly presser
articles.body:
Each week at the Woody Hayes Athletic Center, Ohio State head coach Ryan Day meets with the media ahead of the Buckeyes' matchup that following weekend. Each week here at Land-Grant Holy Land, we will be bringing you three of the biggest storylines from said press conference.

These are three takeaways from Day's Week 7 press conference recapping the game against Maryland and previewing the matchup against Indiana on Saturday at 12 noon ET.

One of the biggest questions heading into this weekend's contest is the health of the Ohio State roster.

Against Maryland, the Buckeyes were without several key players, including six starters.

On offense, tackles Phillip Daniels and Austin Siereveld were both absent, as well as wide receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss. Defensively, corner Jay Timmons missed a second straight game, while linebacker Christian Alliegro and defensive lineman Khary Wilder were also out with undisclosed injuries.

Based on the comments from Day both in his weekly presser and on his Monday appearance on the Buckeye Roundtable show, it does sound like several of those players are expected back for the Indiana game.

Of that group, the three guys most likely to suit up on Saturday are Daniels, Timmons, and McCuin.

Daniels has missed each of the last four games after suffering an injury against Texas, and it feels like he could have returned against the Terrapins if that were a game that was expected to be more hotly contested. Instead, Ohio State was able to give him an extra week to get healthy, and the Buckeyes expect to have their starting right tackle back.

Timmons and McCuin were both game-time decisions against Maryland, and both went through pregame warm-ups with the team before ultimately sitting out. Timmons was in uniform while McCuin was not, leading to believe that he is closer to playing, but it feels as though both were held out for precautionary reasons against an overmatched team in bad weather and should be good to go for the Hoosiers.

The other guys are still a bit of a question mark.

Alliegro was a late add to the injury report this past week, and the nature of his injury is unknown. The same goes for Wilder, who also did not play against Iowa despite having no injury designation the week prior. The Buckeyes would love to have both ready to go against a dynamic Indiana offense.

Siereveld is by far the most curious case, as his absence against Maryland was described by Day as a 'non-football illness' and his timeline to return as "day-to-day." Ohio State would love to have both he and Daniels back for this Saturday, especially after Indiana racked up five sacks the last time these two teams met in the Big Ten title game.

2) Offense has 'made progress' in the red zone, but still looking for more

A key factor in almost all of Ohio State's recent losses against top teams has been a failure to capitalize in the red zone.

Most recently against Texas, the Buckeyes' red zone struggles cropped up right away. Ohio State began with the ball inside the Longhorns' 20-yard line after a fumble on the first offensive play of the game, and yet they could only muster a field goal after a 6-play, 11-yard drive. They would go on to lose by a single point.

In Ohio State's last three losses to Indiana, Miami and Texas, the Buckeyes have scored touchdowns on only five out of 11 trips inside the red zone. A 45.5% mark is just not going to get the job done against these top-tier opponents.

Ohio State has made some strides this season to improve in that area, if nothing else, at least aesthetically.

Arthur Smith has done a good job of transitioning away from the Buckeyes' maddening 13-personnel looks, keeping the team's best players — its wide receivers — on the field. When Smith has decided to go heavy, they have often instead gone to the 'Bison' package, installing an extra offensive lineman rather than a tight end.

It has been an effective strategy, but the team is still not nearly where they'd like to be.

Through six games this season, Ohio State ranks 60th nationally in red zone scoring percentage at 86.7%. The Buckeyes have scored touchdowns on 21-of-30 red zone trips with five field goals, including a perfect 3-for-3 on touchdowns against Maryland last time out.

All too often last season, Ohio State was putting a billion (bad) tight ends on the field in the red zone seemingly just for the sake of it, banging their heads against the wall over and over again as it consistently failed to work. The Buckeyes ' short-field issues are far from fixed, but they have not looked completely hopeless as they have in the past.

With points likely at a premium against Indiana — and over the next several weeks as Ohio State enters a gauntlet of a second-half schedule — you cannot afford to leave points off the board when you've already done most of the hard work to get the ball inside the 20.

Ohio State fans have been clamoring for more Legend Bey ever since his electric touchdown in Week 1 against Ball State.

The speedy freshman put up 74 yards of total offense and the score in the season opener, but since then has played only nine total snaps. Some of Bey's absence was the result of a tweaked ankle suffered against Kent State, but the rest has been earning the trust of the coaches.

This past weekend against Maryland, we finally saw Bey back in action after playing zero offensive snaps against Illinois or Iowa. It wasn't a heavy workload against the Terrapins by any stretch, totaling four carries for 13 yards and also returning a pair of kickoffs for 46 yards, but it was a step in the right direction.

In his Tuesday presser, Day alluded to Bey being back on the right track.

"He's taken some steps in the right direction, for sure, and he's built some momentum. So we'd like to have another good week with him."

Whether for on-field or off-field issues, it's clear that Bey was in the doghouse for a few weeks, and has since done enough to earn his way out of it. Now the question becomes what can he provide the Ohio State offense, and how much will the Buckeyes factor him in against big opponents like this upcoming weekend against Indiana?

Day and his staff have never really been the type to 'save' certain plays or concepts for later in the season. The Buckeyes are not in the business of dialing up trick plays or breaking tendencies to catch an opponent off guard, for better or worse.

That said, Bey might be the type of player who could force their hand.

We have seen a flash of what the freshman can do with the ball in his hands. There is very little film out there of the Texas native at Ohio State, which could play into the Buckeyes' advantage. Could we see some kind of special package for Bey in Bloomington this weekend, or is that level of trust still not quite there?

The Ohio State offense has been starving for explosive plays outside of Jeremiah Smith, and maybe Bey can provide just that in a big moment on the biggest stage.

articles.title: Browns AFC North chances after Week 5 loss
articles.summary: The Browns issues in the lost to the Jets may affect their ability to contend in the AFC North and for the playoffs.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns' loss to the New York Jets snapped their three-game winning streak and dropped their record to 3-2. It was definitely a setback in a part of the schedule that should have featured a very winnable game. One loss this early in the season doesn't eliminate the team's hopes of making a push for the playoffs , but it is certainly a setback.

The Baltimore Ravens now hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North at 4-1 and are favored on the road over the Browns in Week 6 , while the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati Bengals, and Browns are all tied at 3-2. The division looks to be competitive this season, and any mistake or misstep could be the difference between winning the division and falling short.

Cleveland takes on the Ravens in Week 6, so the game could shake up the current standings. FanDuel has the orange and brown among the lowest odds to make the playoffs in the AFC , despite their winning record, not exactly a glowing statement about expectations for Week 6 and beyond.

The Browns will need to execute on offense to avoid putting their defense in a tough position against Baltimore's talented offense. If Cleveland can get back on track in this game, they will still be considered a contender in the division.

Let me know what you think in the comments – Does this loss affect the Browns' ability to contend in the AFC North?

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles fans flock to the bar that brings the City of Brotherly Love to London
articles.summary: Over the past week, London has played host to tens of thousands of Philadelphians and, in Passyunk Avenue, they have a home away from home.
articles.body: Close your eyes, tap your heels together three times and think to yourself there’s no place like home. These were the instructions given to Dorothy as she left the Land of Oz before waking up at home in Kansas. It all seems rather straightforward, but it could have been very different if she happened to be from the City of Brotherly Love. For an NFL fan from Philadelphia wearing the ruby slippers, if they weren’t careful, they may have unexpectedly ended up right in the middle of London, and even then, it might have taken them a bit longer than you’d think to work that out. Over the past week, the English capital has played host to tens of thousands of Philadelphians and, in Passyunk Avenue, they certainly have a home away from home. ‘We need a place that sells cheesesteaks’ When JP Teti moved to London from South Philadelphia, he noticed there were a couple of things his new home was missing. His idea was to kill these two birds with one stone. “I loved living in London. I noted how diverse it was, how you get people from all over the world, and how you could get food from everywhere. But I noticed you couldn’t get, like, this unique regional Philadelphia cuisine,” Teti explained to CNN Sports. The thought that he may never be able to get a hoagie, a cheesesteak or good buffalo wings started weighing heavily on his mind. And it wasn’t just the food that was missing an American touch. After spending much of his late 20s and early 30s in traditional English pubs, Teti also noticed the lack of a real dive bar in the city – a staple in the US. “Philly has great examples of dive bars, and I noted that while the pub is great, the dive bar is great too – in a different way – and that whole idea doesn’t really exist here. And I thought it might be cool if that idea existed.” It could have been easy for Teti to simply dream about this elaborate scheme, but as his career at his “overpaid, underworked corporate job” began to progress, he realized he may never have a better time to bring this idea to life. “For many months now, I’m shooting off my mouth: ‘We need a place that sells cheesesteaks, we need a dive bar, we need a place we can watch football and eat buffalo wings,’” Teti said. “I was thinking, if I don’t act on this, people are going to think I’m all talk and no action.” The next step was selling the idea to his wife, who was also seven months pregnant with their first child. “She looked at me very seriously, but she’s from the Philly area, so she gets it. She gets exactly what I was talking about. She was like, ‘Yeah, let’s do it.’” The following Monday, Teti quit his job and started working on the project that would become Passyunk Avenue. ‘An outpost of hope’ After years of perfecting recipes, working on markets and selling Philadelphian cuisine out of a food truck, Teti reached another crucial juncture on his journey. “I’m either going to stop doing this, or I’m going to bring to fruition what I imagined I wanted this business and brand to be from the very beginning,” Teti outlined to CNN Sports. “These culturally immersive, experiential American-style dive bars that served really authentic American regional cuisine, but more importantly, provided a really interesting cultural exchange for people who were interested in Americana.” The first Passyunk Avenue opened in Fitzrovia in 2018, a year that Philadelphians are particularly fond of. “The Eagles came in October of that year. They brought the Lombardi Trophy – because they just won the Super Bowl – to the original Passyunk, and the rest is history. “It’s like the legend started from there, and we’ve grown to five sites in London now.” Passyunk Avenue fills the market for what Teti calls “Americana-curious Europeans.” “Despite how difficult we make it for people to like us, there’s still a big attraction among large segments of the population of Europe to be attracted to Americana,” he said. “Whether it’s the aspirational nature of it, the enthusiastic nature of it, or the positive nature of the culture.” While the cost of living continues to surge, political tensions rise and times are challenging in both the United Kingdom and the US, Teti hopes that his bars can provide people with an escape. “Passyunk is keeping the light on,” he said. “For all those people who for their own personal reasons have been attracted to the lifestyle and the culture, we’re trying to keep that real. We’re trying to keep that available, and we’re trying to be a bit of an outpost of hope for people.” ‘It feels like we’re in Philly’ Alongside the food and the atmosphere, sport is also a key piece of the Passyunk puzzle. “Since sports is such an important part of the Philadelphia culture, right? It is such a great vehicle to tell the story of the culture,” Teti said. “You can’t talk about the culture of Philadelphia and what it is to be a Philadelphian and experience life in Philadelphia without talking about the narrative of sports.” This past week and a half proved that folks from Philly do really show up for sport. London had become home to Philadelphia Eagles fans from all around the world and they flocked to Passyunk Avenue. The bars put on various events throughout the week, including turning the Leake Street Arches in Waterloo into its own version of Philadelphia’s Reading Terminal Market and hosting a tailgate party outside Passyunk Avenue before the Eagles took on the Jacksonville Jaguars on October 11. “It’s awesome, it feels like we’re in Philly,” one fan told CNN Sports at the tailgate. “This entire week, I’ve been saying ‘Go Birds!’ on the street.” Tailgates aren’t something that London is used to putting on, but you wouldn’t have known that if you happened to stumble across Cleveland Street that day. The smell of freshly made cheesesteaks wafted through the waves of retro jerseys, pints flowed freely and constant chants of “E-A-G-L-E-S!” filled the air as resident DJ Adam Lovelock got the crowd hyped for the big game. Multiple fans mentioned it was just like being at home. But just like in sport, good things take time. Teti still remembers a day where he thought the dream could be over before it even started. “I was down in my railway arch after a particularly sh***y day of street trading, all alone, and thinking maybe no one’s ever going to know that this existed and this might just peter out, and that’ll be that.” Fast forward to February 2025 and Passyunk Avenue hosted a Super Bowl tailgate as thousands saw the Philadelphia Eagles beat the Kansas City Chiefs. “To think back about how lonely I was and how much doubt I had in my head about whether anyone would ever care that I was doing this, and then to think forward to the experience of looking over a crowd that you can’t even see the end of, and be like, ‘Wow, Passyunk put these people here, and Passyunk has brought these people together and made these people care about this.’ That’s when you know it’s all been worth it.” So, as it turns out, maybe Glinda the Good Witch was wrong. Maybe, there are places just like home after all.

articles.title: Roman Reigns Reveals His Mount Rushmore, The Rock Featured amid WWE WrestleMania Rumors
articles.summary: WWE world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns chose four of the biggest stars in the history of the business when asked to name his personal Mount Rushmore for professional wrestling on Wednesday.
articles.body:
WWE world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns chose four of the biggest stars in the history of the business when asked to name his personal Mount Rushmore for professional wrestling on Wednesday.

During an appearance on Club Shay Shay with Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end Shannon Sharpe (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), Reigns named Hulk Hogan, "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, The Rock and John Cena as his Mount Rushmore picks.

Reigns explained the rationale behind his choices, saying, "Everybody always divides it up, like money drawers and ringers. To me, the only one thing—only one metric matters. The money. You know what I mean? And it's show business. The first day I went around the ring, my dad told me, 'Don't ever be confused. This ring is only about money. It's a business. Don't treat it any other way.'"

Predicting Survivor Series Participants 🔮

Ranking Reigns' Biggest Heavyweight Threats 🫡

The OTC went on to express his belief that Hogan, Austin, The Rock and Cena each changed the pro wrestling business in their own unique ways.

"And those guys, I mean, when it came to the money and shifting the business and completely, you know what I mean, just changing the view of it, the optics of it, they all had their own way of doing that," Reigns said. "And they were all critical. We wouldn't be here today without those four, for sure. Many other men go into that category, and women for that matter, but those are kind of, to me, those are the big ones."

Hogan made WWE a household name in the mid-1980s and stayed on top into the early 1990s until his departure. He continued to draw in a massive way upon turning heel in WCW in 1996.

Meanwhile, Austin and The Rock are chiefly responsible for the explosion in popularity experienced by WWE during the Attitude Era in the late 1990s.

Cena essentially took the torch from Austin and The Rock, serving as the face of the company from shortly after the Attitude Era until Reigns' emergence as the unquestioned top guy in around 2020.

Hogan passed away last year, Cena is retired, and Austin is essentially retired, although he did come out of retirement for a match against Kevin Owens at WrestleMania 38 in 2022.

The Rock competed more recently at WrestleMania 40, teaming with Reigns to beat Cody Rhodes and Seth Rollins in the Night 1 main event.

Ever since then and even before, fans have speculated on a potential Reigns vs. The Rock match at WrestleMania.

However, Fightful Select (h/t Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp ) reported last month that WWE is "operating on the assumption that The Rock will not be available" for WrestleMania 43 in Saudi Arabia in April 2027.

With that in mind, the onus is on Reigns, Rhodes and other current stars to put WWE on their back and carry it into the future, much like Reigns' Mount Rushmore picks did in the past.

articles.title: Roman Reigns Addresses Criticism, New WWE Rumors on 946 and TNA Champ Leon Slater
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reigns Discusses Fan Criticism, Regrets, More

Predicting Survivor Series Participants 🔮

As one of the faces of WWE for well over a decade, Roman Reigns has faced his fair share of criticism, but he attempted to put things into perspective this week.

During an appearance Wednesday on Club Shay Shay with Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end Shannon Sharpe (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), Reigns talked about the lighter work schedule he has employed in recent years, particularly in relation to untelevised live events.

Reigns noted that while he regularly worked between 150 and 200 shows per year earlier in his career, it no longer makes sense for him to do that based on the risk of injury and the value lost by the company if he is out of action.

"We're trying to get that back," Reigns said. "I think we're trying to run more live events, and they are good. But we're just at a business model where TV rights are TV rights, and there's just so much money on the line that we got to that point where it's just like, it doesn't make sense for me to do live events anymore. What if I got hurt?

"You know, there's so much money that's riding on Mondays and Fridays and our PLEs now that I can't just go out there and wrestle for, you know, 4,000, 5,000 only, just for those eyes only. Right now, I gotta conserve it."

Reigns also spoke with Sharpe (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News) about the infancy of his WWE career and whether he has any regrets from that time.

The OTC acknowledged that the one thing he wishes he did more often back then was speaking up when he didn't feel creative decisions made sense for him and his character.

"I probably would've said no a few more times early on," Reigns said. "But I just didn't have the equity within the company. I wasn't rooted well enough in the main event scene. I was still auditioning. I was still proving myself. I was still earning that equity."

Reigns even mentioned the infamous "suffering succotash" promo he cut in 2015, saying, "This was like 14 years ago, and they'll still quote me for saying 'suffering succotash.' You know what I mean? This was so long ago. It was 12 years ago. I've delivered unbelievable work since then, but still, I'll be tied to that."

The world heavyweight champion went on to say that there are "two or three promos or scenarios, segments, or finishes of a match" that he would change if he could go back in time and do it over again.

Even so, there is no denying the remarkable career Reigns has carved out for himself, highlight by seven world title runs, numerous WrestleMania main events and some of the most memorable matches and rivalries of his generation.

Reigns overcame fan backlash early in his career that might have sunk lesser performers, but he rose above it and established himself as an all-time great.

Backstage Rumors on 946 and Hayes' Inclusion

The 946 stable continued their dominance Monday night on Raw, as they left The Bloodline laying and added another new member.

In the main event of Raw, which pitted Royce Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price against Solo Sikoa and The Usos, The Bloodline felt the wrath of 946.

Carmelo Hayes shockingly joined 946 when he showed up and hit Sikoa with a crowbar. That led to 946 decimating all three Bloodline members, and the show ending with Keys, Nima, Price, Hayes and Jaida Parker standing tall.

According to False Finish , WWE officials are pleased with how 946 has been presented, and they feel the group has "knocked it out of the park" thus far.

False Finish added that Hayes joining the group has been part of the plan since back in July.

On Sunday, speculation ran rampant on social media that Hayes was potentially on his way out of WWE.

That is due to the fact that Hayes blacked out his profile pic of X, along with AEW star MJF posting an old photo of himself and Hayes facing each other in a match on the independent scene:

However, Melo showed up just a day later on Raw, joining 946 and inserting himself into the biggest storyline in WWE.

Per PWInsider.com (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), WWE purposely kept Hayes out of the spotlight in recent weeks and months in an effort to make his surprise appearance more impactful.

Hayes had not competed in a WWE match since the Aug. 14 episode of SmackDown when he lost a United States Championship bout against Baron Corbin.

His absence from WWE programming since then got people talking, but it was reportedly always part of the company's larger plan to align him with 946.

WWE Reportedly Keeping Tabs on Leon Slater

After Leon Slater beat Nic Nemeth for the TNA World Championship last weekend at Bound For Glory, WWE is reportedly monitoring Slater's situation.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t Mukherjee ), WWE is interested to see what happens with Slater's TNA contract since it is currently believed his deal is set to expire at the end of 2026.

WWE reportedly feels Slater could either drop the title quickly and leave TNA at the end of the year, or sign a short extension before dropping it a bit further down the line, much like Cruz Montana.

Either way, people in WWE have reportedly long expected Slater to eventually sign with the company upon departing TNA, likely starting with a run in NXT.

The 22-year-old Slater is one of the brightest, young stars in pro wrestling, and he already has a hugely impressive résumé to his credit, having held the TNA World Championship once and the X-Division Championship twice.

Slater also already has some experience under his belt when it comes to working in WWE because of the partnership between WWE and TNA.

In addition to competing in a handful of matches in NXT, Slater teamed with Je'Von Evans against AJ Styles and Dragon Lee last December at Saturday Night's Main Event, competing on the undercard of John Cena's retirement match.

He also challenged Carmelo Hayes for the United States Championship on SmackDown in January.

Since Slater already has some roots in WWE, it may only be a matter of time before he officially makes the leap, just like several other TNA stars before him.

articles.title: Ronaldo’s among three Saudi Arabia games postponed due to Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Saudi Pro League postpones three matches after Houthi attacks, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia’s football league has postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr team, following the dramatic escalation in the threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthis.

The Saudi Pro League’s (SPL) matchweek nine fixtures have been pushed back in the calendar for “logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches”, according to a statement published late on Tuesday on the SPL website.

The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo’s Al Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.

The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures “will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes”.

On Monday, Al Nassr’s AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.

Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive in Yemen to retake coastal territory from the Houthis in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.

The latest round of fighting was triggered after two separate strikes that hit Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport left 14 people dead and hundreds injured, and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

Reporting from the Qatari capital Doha, Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi said any notion that the Saudi-led coalition could contain the conflict to Yemen had been shattered over the last 10 days, which saw the targeting of several sites in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said on Wednesday that one person was injured by falling debris after the kingdom downed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh.

Yemen’s Houthis are threatening to keep targeting Saudi airports and oil sites in the coming days, with their attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran and Riyadh adding to the assault on King Khalid International Airport.

articles.title: Saudi tennis ‘slam’ with Alcaraz, Djokovic postponed amid Houthi attacks
articles.summary: The Six Kings Slam exhibition tournament has been pushed from October to December by Saudi organisers.
articles.body:
An exhibition tennis tournament featuring the world’s top men’s players has been postponed for two months by the organisers in Saudi Arabia as the country reels from a spate of attacks by Yemen’s Houthis .

Turki al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority (GEA), said on Wednesday that the exhibition Six Kings Slam tennis tournament had been postponed due to “organisational and logistical challenges”.

The announcement came shortly after the Saudi Pro League postponed three fixtures , including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr, for “logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches”.

The Six Kings Slam was due to hold its third edition later this month, with tennis stars including Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev due to take part alongside Taylor Fritz, Learner Tien and Alex de Minaur.

The event, originally scheduled for October 21-24 and to be streamed live by Netflix, will now take place from December 27-30.

“The Six Kings Slam tournament has been postponed due to logistical reasons and will now take place on December 27,” al-Sheikh said on X, sharing a statement from the Riyadh Season entertainment programme.

Earlier on Wednesday, the three SPL matches involving teams based in Saudi capital Riyadh were postponed.

The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.

The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures “will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes”.

The move comes two days after al-Sheikh promised that boxing’s world title fight featuring Saul “Canelo” ‌‌Alvarez and Christian M’billi will go ahead this month.

Alvarez vs M’billi is scheduled for October 31 in the Saudi capital, which has repeatedly come under attack from Yemen’s Houthis, but al-Sheikh sought to allay the doubts over the bout on Sunday.

“Canelo reached out ⁠⁠and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” al-Sheikh wrote in a social media post. “He [Alvarez] fears nothing.”

On Monday, Al-Nassr’s AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.

Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive in Yemen to retake coastal territory from the Houthis in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia’s sporting programme has been heavily hit since the outbreak of the United States and Israel’s war on Iran in late February.

The Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix slated for April in Jeddah was cancelled.

The WTA Finals were also scheduled to be held in Riyadh next month, but will instead take place at Indian Wells in the US.

articles.title: Lucas Raymond Demoted to Third Line Amid Goal Drought
articles.summary: Todd McLellan dropped Lucas Raymond to the third line Wednesday after 13 straight games without a goal. #RedWings
articles.body:
Detroit Red Wings winger Lucas Raymond has scored zero goals and has recorded four assists, along with a plus/minus rating of minus-4, in six games played this season for Detroit. Raymond has been goalless for 13 straight games dating back to the 2025-26 NHL season, with his last goal coming April 2 at Philadelphia.

With him being in a goalless drought, head coach Todd McLellan demoted him from the first line to the third line on Wednesday morning during practice. Raymond being on the third line could be a wake-up call for him.

New Detroit Red Wings lines with Lucas Raymond demoted to the third line

Ansar Khan of mlive.com was at Red Wings practice on Wednesday. Viktor Arvidsson, Dylan Larkin, and Nate Danielson are the new first line after Raymond was demoted. The second line of Alex DeBrincat, Emmitt Finnie, and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard stays intact.

The new third line features Michael Rasmussen, Andrew Copp, and Raymond. The fourth line features Sheldon Dries, J.T. Compher, and Keegan Kolesar. Hopefully, this shakeup will wake up Raymond and end his goalless drought to begin the 2026-27 NHL season.

Despite being demoted to the third line, Raymond is still on the first power-play unit for now. Larkin, Arvidsson, DeBrincat, and Moritz Seider are the other players on the first power play unit for Detroit. This season, the Red Wings are converting on 20 percent of power play opportunities.

McLellan has not given up on Lucas Raymond

Keeping Raymond on the top power-play unit tracks with what McLellan said about him a day before the demotion. "He's been attempting to get more there, I think this year, than last year. He's been a little bit snakebitten; there were a couple of really good power play shots that, even in Montreal, the goaltender made an outstanding save," McLellan said, per Michael Whitaker of The Hockey News . "I think it will come for Lucas. His game has been okay. So, the scoring, it's going to happen eventually."

With the next game being against the Philadelphia Flyers on Thursday, Oct. 15, this could be a golden chance for Raymond to end his drought. The Flyers are the team he scored his last goal against.

articles.title: NJSIAA moves team state wrestling finals, talks 'red-shirting' proposal
articles.summary: Here's what was discussed at the NJSIAA Executive Committee meeting for October.
articles.body:
ROBBINSVILLE – The road to wrestling glory in New Jersey this winter will divert to Phillipsburg.

NJSIAA Executive Director Colleen Maguire announced at the Oct. 14 Executive Committee meeting that the 2027 wrestling team state championships would be hosted by Phillipsburg High School on Feb. 7.

Rutgers, the usual host, had a conflict with a dual meet against Iowa that day. Maguire said Rutgers worked to try to find alternative options, but none could be found.

"Every year we are there [at Rutgers] we are very grateful," said Maguire. "But Phillipsburg is always eager and willing to host."

Phillipsburg, which has a storied wrestling program, hosted the individual state finals in 2021 when most sites were locked up because of COVID concerns. It has also been the host of the girls individual championships before that was moved to Boardwalk Hall in Atlantic City.

The presentation of state legislative liaison Paul Anzano to the committee included notes on two different bills being discussed before the Assembly. The first is a bill that would allow public schools to hire service veterans, discharged honorably, as coaches without having to get a teaching certificate. The NJSIAA is trying to add law enforcement officers to that exception as well.

Anzano discussed a new proposal that would limit an athlete's clock if he/she 'redshirted' before high school, by holding back a year, presumably for athletic advantage. Anzano noted the bill didn't have much support.

But the concept of redshirting, or 'staying back' continues to be a factor in New Jersey high school sports.

Maguire said Pennsylvania put in a rule saying that your four-year athletic clock started when you completed eighth grade, and that – to her knowledge – there hadn't been a lot of push back on the rule.

"I think there is a national backlog in the high school recruiting process," Maguire said. "Now that the NCAA has set the five-for-five rule, I think that will help. It's not just football, you saw it in baseball and basketball. I think in two years high school recruiting will open up again and be better, maybe we will see less of the reclassing to buy time."

The Executive Committee heard the findings of the Mercadien CPA firm that handled the NJSIAA's financial audit. Assets were described as over $6 million, an 11 percent increase, with revenue increasing 5 percent year-over-year.

Maguire, who started her NJSIAA career as the Financial Director, said the organization had 10 months of operating reserve on hand now, which was "pretty healthy."

Maguire said the organization has used the surplus funds to fully underwrite the Scholar-Athlete luncheon (making it free for all invited) and sent money out to conferences to run local sportsmanship seminars.

She also noted that wrestling and football state championship events pay a large chunk of the sports budget and that revenue can be fickle depending on weather and matchups.

Schools in Non-Public B for football have to notify the NJSIAA of their intent to enter the football playoffs by Oct. 15. Maguire has spoken to most schools, but also said she does give leeway if a school makes a compelling argument to drop out at the last minute. The Non-Public A and B football playoffs will be seeded by a committee on Nov. 1

Chief Operating Officer Tony Maselli said that cleared guidelines on the NJSIAA's official heat policy would be delivered to schools in the spring. He also said the NJSIAA was now mandating that ice hockey coaches wear helmets while on the ice for practice.

Chief Compliance Officer Paul Popadiuk said that four football teams and three boys soccer teams were ineligible for the State Tournament because of disqualifications. He also said for the first time to his knowledge there had been a fight among a pair of runners after a cross-country meet requiring disciplinary action.

The NJSIAA is looking for hosts for the District girls wrestling tournaments on Sunday, Feb. 14 that have room to use three mats.

articles.title: Detroit Red Wings Future Uncertain As Alex DeBrincat Signs Seven-Year Extension
articles.summary: News came out of Detroit, Michigan on Wednesday morning, as the Detroit Red Wings made the Alex DeBrincat signing official. DeBrincat has signed a seven-year...
articles.body:
News came out of Detroit, Michigan on Wednesday morning, as the Detroit Red Wings made the Alex DeBrincat signing official. DeBrincat has signed a seven-year extension worth an average annual value of $13 million. That is the biggest contract in franchise history, as the prices for top-end players continue to climb at a quick rate. Let us discuss the contract and what it means for Detroit.

Alex DeBrincat Signing Holds Decent Value, Many Questions Remain

To begin with, this is fair market value for DeBrincat. As a three-time, 40-goal scorer and a player who scores more goals than records assists, a comparison on the market could be Pavel Dorofeyev , who the New York Rangers signed to a seven-year contract worth $11 million per season . DeBrincat could be seen as a more well-rounded Dorofeyev, as he does more than just finish plays. He can break the puck out of the defensive zone at a solid rate and also make plays off the rush well. According to Corey Sznajder, based on his analytics from All Three Zones , DeBrincat ranked in the 95th percentile for zone exits last season, as reported by The Athletic.

DeBrincat will have a no-trade clause for the first four years of his contract, and then a modified no-trade clause for the last three years.

Red Wings Clearly Have No Intention to Tear It Down

The Red Wings have been in a state of turmoil, from Dylan Larkin's trade request to the drawn-out contract situation regarding Simon Edvinsson . However, given the proactiveness in signing DeBrincat early on in the season, it tells us that Detroit does not want to take a step back. This contract was definitely a telltale sign that there is still belief from management that this team can be competitive, especially with players like Lucas Raymond and Moritz Seider locked up long-term.

However, the key is that Detroit has to get its ducks in a row quickly to maximize DeBrincat's value. He will almost be 30 years old by the time the new contract kicks in, meaning his prime years could come to an end rather early in his contract. The team cannot afford to shoot itself in the foot as it did with the Larkin and Edvinsson situations. The locker room needs to be clear of any and all distractions to be successful.

Can the Red Wings turn things around? Management certainly believes so. It all depends on how the Larkin and Edvinsson situations resolve themselves. Perhaps Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff did not want to have another tough situation on his hands, so he got the DeBrincat signing done early. This move could pay off, but if the team does not end up improving within the next year or two, this move could also stall an underlying need to retool or, worse, rebuild. Time will tell how this contract pans out.

articles.title: Wolves striker Jimenez to have knee surgery
articles.summary: Wolves' veteran striker Raul Jimenez is to have knee surgery - and is now expected to be out of action until January.
articles.body:
Wolves' veteran striker Raul Jimenez has been ruled out until January after learning he needs surgery on his left knee.

The 35-year-old Mexico international has not responded as hoped to treatment for the medial collateral ligament injury he suffered in the Carabao Cup defeat at Everton a month ago and will now have an operation this week.

"Unfortunately Raul's injury has not responded as we expected," said Wolves director of performance Phil Hayward.

"Normally the ligament for a fairly low-grade injury would heal on its own, however this has not responded as we were expecting, and after regularly scanning for the last three weeks, the ligament is not healing in the anticipated way.

"So, he'll have the surgery on Friday in London, and then he'll have around three months of rehabilitation before he's ready to play again."

There is, however, better news on three other injured Wolves players, Rodrigo Gomes (ankle), Bertrand Traore (hamstring) and Boubacar Traore (calf).

Hayward added: "Rodrigo Gomes is progressing well, but it's still early days. He injured a couple of ligaments in the ankle, so it wasn't a straightforward injury

"He's still waiting on the inflammation to settle, and then we'll start to build him up and get him back outside as soon as that's settled. It's not going to be a long-term one, so he should be back reasonably quickly.

"Bertrand Traore has had a hamstring issue. It's a fairly small injury, however it is in a particularly problematic part of the muscle, which can commonly recur if we're not careful. So, we have to respect that and take our time with it. But it's not a big injury, he's doing really well, working hard and won't be too long."

"Boubacar Traore has been out for a couple of weeks because of a problem with his calf. He's back on the pitch working with the rehab coaches and doing really well. He's progressing nicely and he'll be back in full training in the next week or two. He's responded really well to the treatment."

Wolves are ninth in the Championship table, outside the play-off places on goal difference only, and will be away to Burnley on Friday evening.

articles.title: Abilene Christian adds road game against UTSA to 2027 football schedule
articles.summary: The Abilene Christian Wildcats will take on the UTSA Roadrunners for the first time ever in 2027. Here's more on where and what date they will play.
articles.body:
The Abilene Christian Wildcats announced they have added a game against the UTSA Roadrunners to their 2027 football schedule, per an announcement by ACU vice president for athletics Zack Lassiter.

ACU will travel to face UTSA on Sept. 4, 2027, at the Alamodome in San Antonio.

The game represents the first ever meeting between the Wildcats and Roadrunners on the gridiron.

For Abilene Christian, the matchup against UTSA will also mark the Wildcats' 21st game against an FBS opponent since making the jump to the FCS ranks from NCAA Division II in 2014.

The Roadrunners will be ACU's eighth in-state FBS opponent in program history.

The Wildcats have previously faced Baylor, North Texas, SMU, TCU, Texas A&M, Texas Tech and UTEP on the football field.

ACU is also scheduled to travel to face Texas A&M in 2028.

Abilene Christian will open up the 2027 college football season against the Lamar Cardinals on Saturday, Aug. 28, 2027, at Anthony Field at Wildcat Stadium in Abilene.

The Wildcats will then travel to San Antonio to face UTSA on Saturday, Sept. 4, 2027, at the Alamodome in San Antonio.

ACU's only other scheduled nonconference game for the 2027 season is a road game against the Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks on Saturday, Sept. 18 at Homer Bryce Stadium in Nacogdoches.

articles.title: Warriors storm back for second half comeback in preseason win vs. Lakers, 101-89
articles.summary: After falling down by 19 points, the Warriors stormed back in the second half to secure a comeback win over the Lakers, 101-99.
articles.body:
For the second time since the start of the preseason, the Golden State Warriors suited up agains the Los Angeles Lakers . After the Warriors secured their first preseason win in their first matchup at Chase Center, Tuesday's preseason battle in Las Vegas started off on a different foot.

After a tight first quarter, the Lakers took control in the second frame. Behind 12 second quarter points from Austin Reaves, the Lakers jumped out to a 13 point lead at halftime and continued to stretch their lead into the third quarter. Following a 3-pointer from Reaves, the Lakers held a 70-50 lead with nine minutes remaining in the third quarter.

Despite trailing by 20 points, the Warriors didn't walk away from the table in Las Vegas. Behind Will Richard, Brandin Podziemski and Gui Santos, the Warriors started to rally as the Lakers began to rest their core rotational players. As the fourth quarter started, the Warriors trailed by only four points. In the fourth and final frame, the Warriors didn't show any signs of slowing down.

Richard tallied nine points in the fourth quarter on 3-of-5 shooting from the field with three made 3-pointers. Podziemski added seven fourth quarter points as the Warriors surged ahead of the Lakers, completing the comeback on their way to a 101-89.

Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg continued his impressive summer with 17 points on 5-of-11 shooting from the field with five boards and four assisst in 26 minutes.

Steph Curry played into the second half for the first time in the 2026 preseason, scoring 11 points on 3-of-9 shooting from the field with three made triples to go along with two assists and two rebounds in 23 minutes.

Podziemski finished with 17 points on 6-of-12 shooting from the field and three made 3-pointers with five rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes.

The Warriors will wrap up the preseason on Friday, Oct. 16 against the Portland Trail Blazers at San Francisco's Chase Center.
