articles.title: Hawks in the NFL: Week 5
articles.summary: It was an eventful week for former Hawkeyes in the NFL for a few different reasons.
articles.body:
Week 5 is in the books. We still have three undefeated teams. The Eagles are in serious trouble. The NFC East won zero games this weekend, despite two teams in that division playing one another. Let's take a look back at how former Hawks did this week.

We start here for all the wrong reasons. After LA's 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills in Los Angeles on Monday night, Jackson decided that was a good time to get into an altercation with Buffalo defensive end Bradley Chubb. The altercation ended with Jackson throwing a right jab into Chubb's jaw.

Jackson is now the recipient of a 2-game suspension. Good work. Come on, Alaric.

LaPorta is the clear tight end winner this weekend after some really quiet games from Noah Fant, TJ Hockenson, and George Kittle. LaPorta caught 5 passes for 88 yards and this insanely wide open touchdown early in the game.

LaPorta's touchdown opened the floodgates in a 7-7 game, as the Lions raced to a 45-14 lead before a late Arizona touchdown made this look closer than it was. On the other side of the ball, Campbell collected 11 tackles.

Noah Fant, TJ Hockenson, and George Kittle

The rest of the tight end quartet were stunningly quiet. Fant and Hockenson went head to head and both ended with identical 1 catch for 7 yards stat lines. It was the Vikings though that came away with the win, 23-13, to join San Francisco and Kansas City as the lone unbeaten teams in the league.

Kittle did slightly better than Fant and Hockenson, finishing San Francisco's impressive 32-29 win over the defending Super Bowl champions with 5 catches for 24 yards.

Hey I forgot about Erick All ! The tight end quintet! All finished Cincinnati's 31-24 win over Miami with 3 receptions for 25 yards. Tory Taylor was busy, punting 4 times for a 53.0 yard average in Chicago's 31-7 loss to Green Bay. Kaleb Johnson had 7 carries for 26 yards for the Packers, while Lukas Van Ness and Nick Niemann had two tackles apiece. Cooper DeJean logged 10 tackles while AJ Epenesa picked up 1 and a pass defended, but the Eagles dropped one of the dumbest games you'll ever see in London, 19-17 to Jacksonville. That was only topped by the silliness that ensued between the Giants and Commanders, a 27-27 tie that featured a colossal mess up from Jayden Daniels. Drew Stevens finished with two made field goals on two attempts but a missed PAT. It should have been three makes and a game winner, but Daniels had other ideas.

articles.title: Capitals rookie Cole Hutson faces off against brother Lane in first for family
articles.summary: Wednesday night will be a proud moment for the Hutson family.
articles.body:
It will be a family affair at Capital One Arena on Wednesday night as the Capitals host the Canadiens.

Brothers Cole and Lane Hutson are set to face off the first time as NHL players, with the Washington rookie welcoming his accomplished older brother to the nation's capital.

Lane, still young himself at just 22, went from a late second-round pick in 2022 to the Calder Trophy winner in 2024-25 with 66 points. He followed it up with 78 points last season and already has six in six games for the Canadiens this season.

Cole, meanwhile, is just starting to scratch the surface in his NHL career.

Here's what you need to know about the Hutson brothers facing off for the first time.

Cole Hutson faces off with brother Lane Hutson

Ahead of his first NHL matchup with his brother, Lane Hutson told NHL.com's Tom Gulitti that, while it will be "just another game," he is excited for the family first.

"It will be cool, for sure, but it's just going to be another game," Lane said. "We've got to find a way to get some wins. Yeah, it will be cool for me and my brother. But I'm excited for it.

Cole, meanwhile, told Gulitti he hopes the many battles with his brother over the years pay off.

"I've been battling him my whole life, so I kind of know what he's going to do," Cole said. "And, hopefully, we come out with the win."

The Hutson brothers both played for Boston University, but they narrowly missed each other; Lane played for the Terriers in 2022-23 and 2023-24, while Cole played in 2024-25 and 2025-26. The two also narrowly missed each other while playing for the U.S. National Developmental Team.

Both Hutson brothers were second-round picks, but it didn't take too long for either to break through in the NHL. Lane is already a highly-valuable defenseman in Montreal, and the early returns for Cole are strong. The rookie defenseman posted 10 points in his first 14 NHL games last season, and he has a goal and two assists early this season.

Perhaps one day they can play alongside each other in the NHL, but the Canadiens and Capitals are both thrilled with the Hutson they have right now; Lane signed an eight-year, $70.8 million extension with Montreal in 2025.

articles.title: How Texas offensive transfers are performing
articles.summary: CJ Baxter has more rushing yardage than Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown combined.
articles.body:
CJ Baxter has eight rushing touchdowns for a 5-1 Kentucky Wildcats team. Trey Owens has thrown every pass the Arkansas State Red Wolves have attempted. Neto Umeozulu has started all six games for the North Texas Mean Green, and several other former Texas Longhrons offensive linemen have moved into starting lineups at their new schools.

Others are still waiting for a bigger role.

Here's how all 17 offensive players who left Texas after last season are doing, and where each stands on his new team's depth chart.

Owens is getting the playing time that eluded him in Austin. He earned the starting role for head coach Butch Jones and has has thrown all 176 of Arkansas State's passes this season, completing 121 for 1,461 yards with nine touchdowns and six interceptions, and he has run for 149 yards and two scores.

His biggest night came last week against South Alabama, led by former Texas quarterback and assistant Major Applewhite. Owens completed 32-of-43 passes for 418 yards, four touchdowns, and two interceptions in a 56-49 home loss. The Red Wolves are 2-4 and 0-2 in Sun Belt play.

Baxter leads Kentucky with 484 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns on 87 carries, a 5.6-yard average. That's more than the combined yardage of Texas running backs Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown. The former No. 1 running back in the 2023 recruiting class has also caught seven passes for 62 yards, giving him 546 yards from scrimmage for a 5-1 team that has won back-to-back overtime games against South Carolina and LSU.

In the win over the Tigers, Baxter had a 77-yard run, the longest of his career.

Jason Patterson is second on the team with 361 rushing yards, averaging 7.7 yards on 47 carries. Baxter has 40 more carries and five more rushing touchdowns than Patterson.

Wisner has a supporting role in Florida State's backfield. Through six games he has 29 carries for 141 yards and eight catches for 95 yards, without a touchdown. That is second among the Seminoles' running backs in carries, well behind Ousmane Kromah's 100 attempts for 565 yards and five scores. Wisner has also played 27 snaps on special teams.

Kromah started Florida State's 44-20 loss at Louisville on October 9. Wisner ran seven times for 20 yards and caught two passes for 19 that night. The Seminoles are 3-3.

Gibson has appeared in all six of Purdue's games without a start. He has 18 carries for 58 yards and two catches for 14 yards, with no touchdowns.

Fame Ijeboi has started every game and has 117 carries, and Antonio Harris has 23. Fourteen of Gibson's carries came in Purdue's three non-conference games and his longest run went for nine yards. In three Big Ten games, he has four carries for 14 yards.

Clark has played in all six of South Carolina's games as a reserve, with 13 carries for 57 yards and two catches for 14 yards. All of it came in the first three games. In SEC play, Clark has only played 14 snaps, carrying the ball once for one yard against Mississippi State.

Four other Gamecock running backs have more rushing yards.

Stewart has been a reserve in his first season in Nacogdoches. His individual rushing line shows 17 carries for 44 yards in four appearances, without a touchdown. The Tyler Chapell Hill product has played 28 snaps this season.

Jaylen Jenkins, Speedy Jones, and Preston Alford have each run for more than 280 yards in a deep SFA backfield. The Lumberjacks were unbeaten entering their open date last weekend.

The former Texas walk on appeared in seven games over four seasons at Texas. He has played in three for North Texas, against Houston Christian, Tulsa and Charlotte, and got his first carries in the October 10 win over Charlotte: three runs for eight yards. Page has also played 17 snaps on special teams.

Jahiem White leads the Mean Green backfield with 687 yards and nine touchdowns on 96 carries and has started all six games. Page is not listed on North Texas' most recent depth chart, issued for the Charlotte game, which has White, Brendon Haygood, and then Nick Osho or Adarion Nettles at running back.

Moore has started all five of Colorado's games at receiver and is second on the team with 18 catches for 242 yards and a touchdown, behind Joseph Williams' 32 receptions for 454 yards. His best day was a four-catch, 107-yard game with a touchdown against Weber State. He was held without a catch at Baylor.

Colorado is 2-3 and was idle October 10. Julian Lewis started the first four games at quarterback, and Isaac Wilson made his first Colorado start against Texas Tech on Oct. 3. Moore is listed first at one receiver spot on Colorado's depth chart for its October 17 game against Utah.

Butler caught one pass in four games over two seasons at Texas. Through six games at Oregon State, he has 13 catches for 190 yards and a touchdown, plus four carries for 56 yards and another score. That score, a 30-yard run in the October 3 win at Colorado State, was the first rushing touchdown of his career.

He started at receiver alongside Jesse Legree and Bubba Hampton in the 66-14 win over San Diego State on Oct. 10 and caught two passes for 35 yards. Hampton, a one-time Texas commit, has 20 catches for 245 yards and one touchdown. The Beavers have won four straight after an 0-2 start.

Livingstone started against his former team in Oklahoma's 27-24 win over Texas on October 10, playing 29 snaps without receiving a target. Through the Sooners' first five games, he has six catches for 51 yards and no touchdowns. His receiving numbers trail Isaiah Sategna III, Rocky Beers, Trell Harris, and Hayden Hansen.

Ffrench has yet to catch a pass through Michigan's first five games, playing just 18 snaps. He appeared as a reserve against Minnesota on Oct. 3, when JJ Buchanan, Andrew Marsh and Salesi Moa started at receiver, and the Wolverines were idle October 10.

Receivers coach Micah Simon said earlier that week that Ffrench had practiced well and could earn more opportunities, according to On SI .

Washington has no receptions in North Carolina's season statistics and is yet to appear in a game this season. RotoWire reported that an undisclosed injury kept him out of the October 3 game against Notre Dame, and ACCSports' final availability report listed him out again for the October 10 game against Pittsburgh.

Jelani Thurman has become the Tar Heels' leading receiving tight end.

Stroh opened the season in a rotational role and has worked his way into Kansas' starting lineup. The Jayhawks moved him ahead of Amir Herring at left guard before the October 3 game against Middle Tennessee, according to KU Sports, and he started again at Utah on October 10. The promotion gives him a starting job after three seasons at Texas.

Against the Utes, Stroh allowed two quarterback hits and two hurries while committing two penalties, grading at 31.8 in pass blocking, according to Pro Football Focus.

Umeozulu has started all six games for 4-2 North Texas. The Mean Green's game-by-game lineup chart lists him at right tackle for the first five before moving to left guard last week. He is the first-team right tackle on the team's most recent depth chart. Per PFF, Umeozulu has allowed two quarterback hits and seven pressures while committing five penalties.

He appeared in 26 games over four seasons at Texas without making a start.

Kibble earned Baylor's starting left guard job. The Bears' September 12 depth chart listed him first at left guard, and he was among Baylor's starting offensive linemen in the October 3 win at Arizona State. Baylor was off last week. The 6'3, 333-pounder has allowed one sack, one quarterback hit, and six pressures.

Cruz made his first career start at center against Louisville on October 3 and started again against Wake Forest a week later. His promotion came amid injuries on NC State's offensive line, including to center Spike Sowells, and he played every offensive snap against Louisville, according to local reporting. He has gone from a reserve role to the starting lineup during ACC play, playing well as a pass blocker with only one quarterback hit allowed, but he has also committed two penalties.

Brooks has appeared in all six of Alabama's games as a reserve, splitting his work between special teams and limited snaps on the offensive line. His Alabama biography, updated through October 3, credits him with seven snaps on the line against East Carolina, three against Kentucky, and four at left tackle against Mississippi State, plus late offensive work against South Carolina.

He was listed among Alabama's reserves again for the October 10 game against Georgia.

articles.title: Why the Spurs are thrilled to have undersized guard Jordan McLaughlin back
articles.summary: The undersized guard from Southern California re-signed with the team after briefly considering a handful of other offers. His teammates and coaches are more...
articles.body:
It wasn't one of the marquee moves of the offseason, but the Spurs' transaction on July 12 prompted positive reactions all the way from Paris to a peaceful critter-filled spread out in Boerne.

"It put a smile on my face to know he was going to be back with us," Keldon Johnson said.

Indeed, the Spurs re-signing little-used Jordan McLaughlin to a one-year, $3.2 million contract to return as a reliable fourth guard insurance policy was a feel-good moment for all the players and members of the coaching staff.

"He's always ready to play," Johnson said. "He's always positive, just an amazing teammate, an amazing asset, the ultimate professional. He shows up every day. He's consistent. He never wavers. He's never rattled, and he always gives everything he's got."

Said coach Mitch Johnson, "J-Mac has been great for us."

Before agreeing to terms, McLaughlin, 30, briefly looked at joining another team after getting what he called a "couple of other looks" from Atlanta, Boston and Utah.

Underscore "briefly." The eighth-year pro wanted to come back to San Antonio.

"I was very content with staying here," McLaughlin said. "I know what I'm getting. Super happy about the deal, super happy to be back with the guys and the team, the organization."

The 6-foot, 180-pound McLaughlin averaged just 6.4 minutes last season but performed well when called upon while also mentoring younger players, including fellow Southern Californian Carter Bryant, the No. 14 overall pick of the 2026 NBA draft.

"He's such a good guy and his family, his wife are amazing," Bryant said last season. "They're just amazing people, beautiful people, super sweet and genuine. J-Mac is someone I look up to. I mean this in the best way possible, him as a human being is so far beyond him as a basketball player. Just the way he operates, the way he conducts himself. He's a pro's pro. He's never been in a game where you're like, "Bro, we need to get J-Mac out of here.'"

That was true in May when injuries to De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper prompted Mitch Johnson to call on him.

"He got thrown into the Western Conference finals and probably a lot of people were not expecting that," the coach said.

With Fox sidelined for a second straight game with a sore ankle and Harper forced to leave late in the third period with a hamstring injury, McLaughlin logged seven meaningful minutes in Game 2 of the Western Conference finals.

Right off the bat, the Southern Cal alumnus made a play, scoring on a step-back 3 just 32 seconds after he entered the game late in the first period. He hit another shot from beyond the arc in the third to finish with six points on 2 of 3 from the field and one assist in the 122-113 loss.

"Every single time J-Mac comes in, he makes the right play, hits a big shot," Devin Vassell said after the game "As soon as he came in, he wasn't even warm yet and he hits a three. He's steady. If he needs to come in and play, I don't think anybody is worried or concerned."

Like McLaughlin, Mitch Johnson was an undersized point guard during his playing days in Seattle as a prep standout and later at Stanford. He appreciates that McLaughlin is always prepared to go when called upon, which was also the case on Monday night in the 119-109 preseason loss at Utah, when he produced 14 points and six assists in 22 minutes as a starter because of the team's decision to rest Stephon Castle and Harper.

"He executes exactly what you want and plays with composure, and that's all you want as a coach," Mitch Johnson said. "And for him to be able to be back is important. We want a lot of people to be back because of what we experienced last year."

McLaughlin came to the Spurs from Sacramento on Feb. 3, 2025, as part of the three-team trade centered on Fox.

It didn't take long for him to fall in love with the franchise and San Antonio.

"Man, it's just the way they operate," McLaughlin said of the Spurs. "You hear nothing but good things before coming into the organization, but when you're in it and you actually see it, they take care of their players."

He also loves the camaraderie of the locker room.

"The players take care of the players," McLaughlin said. "This is a good group of guys, a very talented group of guys, and we all enjoy each other's company. Enjoy coming into work every single day."

Along those lines, he has fond memories of last season's surprising run to the Finals.

"It was a super fun run, and we're looking to do the same with a better outcome this year," he said. "We are confident and connected. Bringing everybody back and adding a player like Tobias (Harris) is huge for us and I think that'll help boost us to where we want to get to."

His teammates feel the same is true of him.

"It's great when you get a teammate like J-Mac, a professional like J-Mac, who shows up each and every day and does whatever we need him to do," Keldon Johnson said. "You know what you're going to get each and every night."

articles.body:
Free agent attacker Jadon Sancho has this week been linked with what would be an altogether surprising move to Spain, with Getafe.

The brass at the Estadio Coliseum are for their part fresh off tying up a deal for one high-profile free agent, in the form of Dani Carvajal. The veteran defender has penned terms with Getafe through the close of the campaign.

And if the latest word stemming from the media on Wednesday is anything to go by, then the Azulones do not appear done there…

As per a report from Diario Sport , citing DAZN:

'The club's next target is in England: Jadon Sancho. The Madrid club has shown interest in the former Borussia Dortmund, Aston Villa, Manchester United, and Chelsea player to bolster their attack.'

It is added that the operation is considered unlikely to ultimately come to fruition, owing chiefly to Sancho's considerable salary demands. But the Getafe hierarchy nevertheless remain hard at work to clear space on their books, to open up the possibility.
